modules.name: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects
CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the acronym 'CSS' stand for?
questions.b: Cascading Style Sheets
questions.explanation: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets, defining visual presentation for HTML documents.

questions.question: In a standard CSS rule 'h1 { color: red; font-size: 20px; }', what is 'h1' called?
questions.b: The Selector
questions.explanation: The selector points to the HTML element(s) to which the style declarations will apply.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets an element with the HTML attribute id='main-header'?
questions.b: #main-header
questions.explanation: The hash (#) symbol selects elements by their unique ID attribute.

questions.question: Which CSS selector targets all elements with the HTML class 'card-title'?
questions.b: .card-title
questions.explanation: The period/dot (.) symbol selects elements by class name.

questions.question: What does the universal selector '*' select in CSS?
questions.b: All elements of any type in the entire DOM tree
questions.explanation: The universal selector (*) matches every single element in the document.

questions.question:
How do you apply the same CSS styling declarations to

,

, and

simultaneously (Selector Grouping)?
questions.b: h1, h2, p { color: blue; }
questions.explanation: Commas separate multiple grouped selectors sharing the same declaration block.

questions.question: What is the calculated CSS Specificity weight representation for an ID selector (e.g. #nav)?
questions.explanation: Specificity is measured as (Inline, ID, Class/Attribute/Pseudo-class, Element). An ID selector adds (0, 1, 0, 0).

questions.question: What is the Specificity value of a single Class selector (e.g. '.btn')?
questions.explanation: Classes, attributes, and pseudo-classes contribute (0, 0, 1, 0) to specificity.

questions.question: What is the Specificity value of an Element / Type selector (e.g. 'div' or 'p')?
questions.explanation: HTML tag/element selectors and pseudo-elements contribute (0, 0, 0, 1).

questions.question: What happens when two CSS rules with identical specificity target the exact same element property?
questions.a: The first rule in the stylesheet always wins
questions.b: The rule declared LATER (last in source order) takes precedence and overrides the earlier one
questions.d: The browser generates a console error
questions.explanation: Under the Cascade rule, when specificity is equal, the last declared rule in source order wins.

questions.question: What does appending '!important' to a CSS property value declaration do (e.g. 'color: red !important;')?
questions.b: Overrides normal cascading specificity rules, giving the declaration maximum priority
questions.c: Applies the style only in dark mode
questions.explanation: !important overrides standard cascade specificity and inline styles, and should be used sparingly.

questions.question: Where should an external CSS stylesheet link tag '<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">' ideally be placed in an HTML document?
questions.a: Inside the <body> tag at the bottom
questions.b: Inside the <head> section
questions.explanation: Placing stylesheets inside <head> ensures styles are parsed before rendering, preventing Flash of Unstyled Content (FOUC).

questions.question: How are inline styles applied directly to an individual HTML element?
questions.b: Using the 'css' attribute
questions.explanation: The HTML 'style' attribute embeds inline CSS declarations directly onto elements with (1, 0, 0, 0) specificity.

questions.question: Which selector has the highest specificity among the following options?
questions.b: #header .nav-item
questions.explanation: #header .nav-item has 1 ID and 1 Class (0, 1, 1, 0), which beats any number of classes or elements without IDs.

questions.question: What is 'Inheritance' in CSS?
questions.b: The mechanism by which certain property values (like color and font-family) set on a parent element automatically pass down to its descendant children
questions.explanation: Typography and text properties are inherited down the DOM tree unless explicitly overridden.

questions.question: Which CSS keyword explicitly forces a property to take the computed value of its parent element?
questions.b: inherit
questions.explanation: 'inherit' instructs the property to adopt its parent's computed value.

questions.question: What does the 'initial' keyword reset a CSS property value to?
questions.a: The value specified by the browser's user-agent stylesheet
questions.b: The official default value specified in the W3C specification for that property
questions.explanation: 'initial' sets a property to its official CSS specification default value.

questions.question: What does the 'unset' CSS keyword do?
questions.b: Acts as 'inherit' if the property naturally inherits, or acts as 'initial' if it does not
questions.explanation: 'unset' erases declarations, defaulting to inheritance if applicable, or initial otherwise.

questions.question: How do you write comments inside a CSS stylesheet file?
questions.b: /* This is a comment */
questions.explanation: CSS only supports block comments enclosed between /* and */.

questions.question: Which rule imports another external CSS file from within a stylesheet?
questions.b: #include "theme.css";
questions.explanation: The @import at-rule loads external CSS stylesheets into the current file.

questions.question: What is the Specificity value of the ':where()' pseudo-class (e.g. ':where(h1, h2, h3)')?
questions.explanation: :where() always has a specificity of exactly (0, 0, 0, 0), making its declarations easy to override.

questions.question: What is the Specificity value of the ':is()' pseudo-class (e.g. ':is(#header, .nav)')?
questions.b: The specificity of its most specific argument selector in the list
questions.explanation: :is() takes on the specificity of its single highest-weighted argument.

questions.question: Which of the following properties is NOT inherited by default in CSS?
questions.b: font-family
questions.explanation: Box model properties (margin, padding, border, width) are not inherited by children.

questions.question: What does the declaration 'all: unset;' accomplish on an element?
questions.b: Resets all CSS properties on that element back to their initial or inherited values simultaneously
questions.explanation: The 'all' shorthand resets all standard CSS properties on the selector in one command.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'ch' unit in CSS?
questions.a: Width of the '0' (zero) glyph in the current font
questions.b: Height of uppercase 'C'
questions.explanation: 1ch equals the advance measure width of the '0' character in the active font.

questions.question: What is a 'CSS Reset' stylesheet (e.g. Eric Meyer's reset)?
questions.a: A script that reboots the browser
questions.b: A stylesheet that removes all default browser user-agent margins, paddings, and font sizes to ensure cross-browser consistency
questions.c: A tool to minify CSS files
questions.explanation: CSS Resets zero out default browser inconsistencies so layouts render identically across Chrome, Firefox, and Safari.

questions.question: How does 'Normalize.css' differ from a traditional aggressive CSS Reset?
questions.b: It preserves useful browser defaults (like heading sizes and list bullets) while correcting bugs and normalizing styles across browsers
questions.explanation: Normalize.css standardizes styles while retaining semantic element ergonomics.

questions.question: What is the meaning of Case Sensitivity in CSS selectors?
questions.a: CSS property names and values are case-insensitive, but HTML class names and IDs are case-sensitive in standard HTML/XHTML documents
questions.b: Everything in CSS is strictly case-sensitive
questions.explanation: Properties are case-insensitive, but user-defined classes/IDs must match HTML casing.

questions.question: Can an HTML element have multiple class names separated by spaces (e.g. '<div class="card primary shadow">')?
questions.a: No, only one class is permitted per element
questions.b: Yes, and CSS rules for all listed classes apply simultaneously to that element
questions.explanation: Space-separated class lists allow composable utility styling.

questions.question: What does the selector 'p.intro' target?
questions.b:
Only

elements that possess the class 'intro'
questions.explanation:
Compound selector matching

tags with class 'intro'.

questions.question: What does the 6-digit HEX color '#FF0000' represent?
questions.b: Pure Red (Full Red, 0 Green, 0 Blue)
questions.explanation: #RRGGBB format assigns FF (255) to Red and 00 to Green and Blue.

questions.question: What does the 4th parameter 'alpha' represent in 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)'?
questions.b: Opacity / Transparency channel (0 is fully transparent, 1 is fully opaque)
questions.explanation: The alpha parameter modulates layer opacity between 0.0 and 1.0.

questions.question: In the HSL color model 'hsl(120, 100%, 50%)', what do H, S, and L stand for?
questions.b: Hue (0-360 degrees), Saturation (0-100%), Lightness (0-100%)
questions.explanation: HSL models cylindrical color space where 120 deg corresponds to pure green.

questions.question: What does the modern CSS color keyword 'currentColor' refer to?
questions.a: The browser's default link blue color
questions.b: The current computed value of the element's 'color' property
questions.explanation: currentColor cascades the active text color to borders, fills, or shadows dynamically.

questions.question: Which CSS property sets a background image for an element?
questions.b: background-image: url('bg.jpg');
questions.explanation: background-image specifies one or more background image resource URLs.

questions.question: What does 'background-size: cover;' do to a background image?
questions.a: Stretches the image to fit without maintaining aspect ratio
questions.b: Scales the image proportionally so that it completely covers the entire background container, cropping excess edges if necessary
questions.c: Tiles the image across the page
questions.d: Shows the image at 100% natural resolution
questions.explanation: cover scales the image proportionally until both dimensions fill the container completely.

questions.question: What does 'background-size: contain;' do to a background image?
questions.a: Scales the image proportionally so the entire image is visible without cropping, leaving empty letterbox space if aspect ratios differ
questions.b: Crops the image into a circle
questions.explanation: contain fits the complete image inside container boundaries without any cropping.

questions.question: Which CSS property prevents a background image from repeating across the container?
questions.b: background-tile: off;
questions.explanation: background-repeat: no-repeat renders only a single instance of the image.

questions.question: What does 'background-attachment: fixed;' achieve?
questions.a: Locks the background image so it stays fixed relative to the viewport while page content scrolls over it (Parallax effect)
questions.b: Disables background image loading
questions.explanation: fixed attachments anchor images to the viewport for smooth parallax scrolling.

questions.question: Which CSS function creates a smooth linear color transition between two or more colors?
questions.b: gradient-linear(color1, color2)
questions.explanation: linear-gradient() generates procedural gradient image textures along an angle or direction.

questions.question: How do you create a radial gradient emanating from the center in CSS?
questions.b: circle-gradient(red, yellow)
questions.explanation: radial-gradient() blends colors outward from a focal point in circular or elliptical patterns.

questions.question: What does a 'conic-gradient()' create in CSS3?
questions.a: A gradient rotated around a center point (like a color wheel or pie chart)
questions.b: A 3D cone texture
questions.explanation: conic-gradient() rotates color transitions around a central axis (ideal for pie charts).

questions.question: Which CSS property rounds the outer corners of an element's border?
questions.b: border-radius
questions.explanation: border-radius curves the corners (e.g. border-radius: 50% for circles).

questions.question: How do you make an exact circular avatar image from a square 100px by 100px element?
questions.b: border-radius: 50%;
questions.explanation: Setting border-radius to 50% on equal width/height elements renders a perfect circle.

questions.question: What is the shorthand syntax for setting a solid red border of 2px width?
questions.b: border-style: 2px red solid;
questions.explanation: The border shorthand accepts 'width style color' (e.g. 2px solid red).

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'border' and 'outline' in CSS?
questions.a: Outlines take up space in the box model, while borders do not
questions.b: Borders take up space in the element's box model; Outlines are drawn outside the border without taking up layout space or affecting surrounding elements
questions.explanation: Outlines sit on top of elements without triggering reflow or shifting adjacent elements.

questions.question: Which property creates space between an element's border and its outline?
questions.b: outline-offset
questions.explanation: outline-offset pushes the outline outward from the border edge (e.g. outline-offset: 4px;).

questions.question: What does 'background-clip: text;' combined with '-webkit-text-fill-color: transparent;' create?
questions.b: Renders the background image or gradient clipped to the shape of the text letters (Text Gradient effect)
questions.explanation: Clips the background fill directly inside the letter glyph paths.

questions.question: What does 'background-origin' determine in CSS?
questions.a: The server location of the image file
questions.b: The background positioning area: border-box, padding-box, or content-box
questions.c: The aspect ratio of the image
questions.explanation: background-origin defines the reference origin rectangle where background images begin.

questions.question: Which CSS property allows using custom graphic images as a decorative element border?
questions.b: border-graphic
questions.explanation: border-image slices and tiles custom raster or SVG images along border perimeters.

questions.question: What does the CSS property 'box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgba(0,0,0,0.1);' do?
questions.b: Casts a soft drop shadow beneath the element (X-offset 0, Y-offset 4px, Blur 6px, Spread -1px)
questions.explanation: box-shadow renders outer or inset blur shadows around element boxes.

questions.question: How do you make an inset (inner) box-shadow in CSS?
questions.a: Add the 'inset' keyword to the box-shadow declaration (e.g. box-shadow: inset 0 2px 4px black;)
questions.b: Use box-shadow-type: inner;
questions.explanation: The 'inset' token draws shadows inside the frame perimeter.

questions.question: What does the CSS Color 4 function 'oklch()' offer over traditional RGB/HSL?
questions.b: Perceptually uniform lightness and access to wider P3 display color gamuts
questions.explanation: OKLCH delivers uniform perceptual color brightness and ultra-vibrant wide-gamut shades.

questions.question: How do you specify multiple background layers on a single element in CSS?
questions.a: Declare background-image multiple times on separate lines
questions.b: Separate each background image URL with a comma in a single background-image declaration
questions.explanation: Comma-separated layer lists stack backgrounds with the first listed image on top.

questions.question: What is the result of 'border-style: dotted dashed solid double;' on an element's 4 sides?
questions.a: Top: dotted, Right: dashed, Bottom: solid, Left: double (Clockwise order)
questions.b: Top: double, Right: solid, Bottom: dashed, Left: dotted
questions.explanation: 4-value shorthand follows the universal TRBL (Top, Right, Bottom, Left) clockwise order.

questions.question: What does 'border: none;' or 'border: 0;' do to an HTML element (like <input> or <button>)?
questions.b: Removes all default browser borders from the element
questions.explanation: Zeroes out default button/input borders.

questions.question: What does 'background-position: center bottom;' specify?
questions.b: Background image is centered horizontally and anchored to the bottom edge vertically
questions.explanation: Positions the background asset at horizontal center and vertical bottom.

questions.question: What happens when you declare 'opacity: 0.5;' on a parent container?
questions.a: Only the parent background becomes semi-transparent
questions.b: The entire parent element AND all of its child elements become 50% transparent
questions.explanation: Opacity applies to the entire rendered subtree. Use rgba() background colors if children must stay opaque.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'repeating-linear-gradient()' create?
questions.b: A repeating stripe pattern that loops infinitely based on specified color stop pixel intervals
questions.explanation: repeating-linear-gradient() tiles gradient bands for barber-pole and diagonal stripe patterns.

questions.question: What is the default value of the 'background-color' property for HTML elements?
questions.b: transparent
questions.explanation: The default background color is transparent, allowing underlying parent layers to show through.

questions.question: What are the four components of the standard CSS Box Model, from innermost to outermost?
questions.b: Content, Padding, Border, Margin
questions.explanation: The Box Model consists of: (1) Content -> (2) Padding -> (3) Border -> (4) Margin.

questions.question: In the default CSS box model ('box-sizing: content-box;'), what does the 'width' property set?
questions.a: The total width including padding and border
questions.b: The width of the Content area ONLY (padding and borders are added on top, increasing total rendered width)
questions.explanation: In content-box, total width = width + padding-left + padding-right + border-left + border-right.

questions.question: What does 'box-sizing: border-box;' do when applied to elements?
questions.b: Forces 'width' and 'height' to include content, padding, and borders within the specified dimension
questions.explanation: border-box locks total element size so padding and borders do not expand the container.

questions.question: Why is '* { box-sizing: border-box; }' universally adopted in modern CSS architecture?
questions.b: It makes sizing predictable: adding padding or borders never accidentally breaks layouts or causes horizontal overflow
questions.c: It is required for JavaScript to run
questions.explanation: border-box ensures elements adhere strictly to declared widths regardless of internal padding.

questions.question: What is 'Vertical Margin Collapsing' in CSS?
questions.b: When adjacent vertical margins (top and bottom) of block elements combine into a single margin equal to the largest individual margin
questions.explanation: Adjacent top/bottom block margins collapse into the maximum single margin value.

questions.question: Do horizontal margins (left and right) ever collapse in standard CSS flow?
questions.b: No, horizontal margins NEVER collapse; they always sum together
questions.explanation: Horizontal margins are strictly additive and never collapse.

questions.question: In which layout contexts is Vertical Margin Collapsing completely disabled?
questions.a: Inside Flexbox containers, CSS Grid containers, and positioned (absolute/fixed) elements
questions.b: Only on <h1> tags
questions.explanation: Flex items, grid items, floats, and absolute positioned elements never collapse vertical margins.

questions.question: What does 'margin: 0 auto;' do to a block-level element with a specified width?
questions.b: Horizontally centers the block element within its parent container by distributing available left/right space equally
questions.explanation: 'margin: 0 auto' calculates equal auto left/right margins to center fixed-width blocks.

questions.question: What does the 2-value shorthand 'padding: 10px 20px;' mean?
questions.b: Top/Bottom: 10px; Left/Right: 20px
questions.explanation: 2-value syntax sets Vertical (Top/Bottom) first, then Horizontal (Left/Right).

questions.question: What does the 3-value shorthand 'margin: 10px 20px 30px;' represent?
questions.b: Top: 10px, Bottom: 20px, Left/Right: 30px
questions.explanation: 3-value shorthand: Top (1st), Left/Right (2nd), Bottom (3rd).

questions.question: Can 'padding' values be negative in CSS?
questions.a: Yes, negative padding moves content outward
questions.b: No, negative padding values are illegal in CSS and will be ignored by the browser
questions.explanation: Padding cannot be negative. Margins can be negative, but padding must be >= 0.

questions.question: What does a negative margin (e.g. 'margin-top: -20px;') do to an element?
questions.b: Pulls the element upward by 20px, overlapping preceding sibling content
questions.explanation: Negative margins draw elements closer or cause intentional overlap.

questions.question: What happens if you apply vertical padding or vertical margins to a pure inline element (e.g. standard <span>)?
questions.a: The element becomes a block element
questions.b: Horizontal margin/padding works normally, but vertical padding/margin does NOT push surrounding lines away or alter line height
questions.explanation: Inline elements ignore vertical margin pushing; switch to 'inline-block' to affect vertical flow.

questions.question: What does the CSS property 'overflow: hidden;' do to container content that exceeds its dimensions?
questions.b: Clips and hides any overflow content outside the container box without rendering scrollbars
questions.explanation: overflow: hidden truncates spilling content cleanly at container edges.

questions.question: What does 'overflow: scroll;' do?
questions.a: Always displays scrollbars on the container (both horizontal and vertical), even if content does not overflow
questions.b: Hides overflow content
questions.explanation: overflow: scroll forces visible scrollbars regardless of content size.

questions.question: What does 'overflow: auto;' do?
questions.b: Automatically displays scrollbars ONLY when content actually overflows the container boundaries
questions.explanation: overflow: auto introduces scrollbars adaptively when content overflows.

questions.question: What does 'overflow-x: hidden; overflow-y: auto;' configure?
questions.a: Hides vertical scrolling and scrolls horizontally
questions.b: Prevents horizontal overflow while allowing vertical scrolling when content exceeds height
questions.explanation: Separate X/Y axis overflow control prevents accidental horizontal page wobble.

questions.question: What is a 'Block Formatting Context' (BFC) in CSS?
questions.b: An isolated rendering region of the page where block boxes are laid out independently, containing internal floats and preventing margin collapse with outside elements
questions.explanation: BFC creates self-contained layout boundaries (e.g. via overflow: hidden or display: flow-root).

questions.question: Which modern CSS display value establishes a Block Formatting Context without unwanted overflow clipping side-effects?
questions.b: display: bfc;
questions.explanation: 'display: flow-root' creates a clean BFC containing internal floats without hiding overflows.

questions.question: What is the 'Clearfix' hack historically used for in CSS?
questions.b: Forcing a parent container to expand and clear internal floated children so the parent does not collapse to zero height
questions.explanation: Clearfixes (:after { content: ''; display: table; clear: both; }) prevent parent collapse over floats.

questions.question: What does the 'clear: both;' property do on an element?
questions.a: Deletes both left and right margins
questions.b: Prevents the element from sitting adjacent to previous floated elements on either left or right, forcing it below them
questions.explanation: clear: both drops elements below all preceding floating siblings.

questions.question: What is the computed total width of a div with: 'width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; box-sizing: content-box;'?
questions.explanation: In content-box: 200 (width) + 40 (left/right padding) + 10 (left/right border) = 250px.

questions.question: What is the computed total width of a div with: 'width: 200px; padding: 20px; border: 5px solid black; box-sizing: border-box;'?
questions.b: 200px (content area shrinks to 150px to accommodate padding and border within 200px)
questions.explanation: In border-box, total width stays exactly 200px; inner content adjusts to 150px.

questions.question: What does 'max-width: 100%;' on an element ensure?
questions.b: Image will never overflow its parent container width, shrinking responsively if the container becomes narrower than the image natural size
questions.explanation: max-width: 100% is the foundational rule of responsive web imagery.

questions.question: What does 'min-height: 100vh;' do to a page section?
questions.b: Ensures the section is at least as tall as 100% of the viewport height, expanding further if content exceeds it
questions.explanation: min-height: 100vh ensures hero/full-page sections cover the viewport minimum.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'min-width' and 'max-width'?
questions.a: min-width defines a lower boundary (element cannot be narrower); max-width defines an upper boundary (element cannot grow wider)
questions.b: They are identical
questions.c: min-width only applies to mobile devices
questions.explanation: min-width guarantees a minimum width; max-width caps maximum width expansion.

questions.question: How does 'padding-inline' differ from 'padding-left' and 'padding-right' in CSS Logical Properties?
questions.b: It sets padding on the inline start and end (left/right in LTR languages, right/left in RTL Arabic/Hebrew) automatically adapting to writing direction
questions.explanation: Logical properties (padding-inline, margin-block) dynamically adapt to writing modes.

questions.question: What does 'margin-block: 2rem;' set in CSS Logical Properties?
questions.b: Top and bottom margins (the block axis in horizontal writing modes)
questions.explanation: margin-block maps to vertical margins (top and bottom) in standard horizontal typography.

questions.question: What happens when an element has 'height: auto;'?
questions.b: The element's height automatically calculates to fit the natural height of its internal content
questions.explanation: auto calculates container dimensions based on descendant content height.

questions.question: What does 'box-decoration-break: clone;' do for inline text elements spanning across multiple lines?
questions.b: Renders padding, border, and background independently for each fragmented line box as if they were separate elements
questions.explanation: clone repeats border-radius and padding on every line fragment of wrapped inline tags.

questions.question: Which CSS property sets the font family for text elements?
questions.b: font-family
questions.explanation: font-family specifies a prioritized fallback list of font family names and generic family names.

questions.question: Why is a generic font family (e.g. 'sans-serif', 'serif', 'monospace') always placed at the very end of a font stack?
questions.a: It is required by CSS syntax
questions.b: It serves as a universal fallback ensuring the browser renders an appropriate system typeface if custom web fonts fail to load
questions.explanation: Generic fallbacks guarantee visual consistency if custom web font assets fail.

questions.question: What is the key visual distinction between 'Serif' and 'Sans-Serif' typefaces?
questions.a: Serif fonts have small decorative strokes/projections at the ends of letter lines (e.g. Times New Roman); Sans-Serif fonts have clean, plain stroke ends (e.g. Arial)
questions.b: Sans-Serif fonts are always bold
questions.c: Serif fonts can only be used in print
questions.d: Sans-Serif fonts cannot have italic styles
questions.explanation: Serifs are traditional decorative feet; sans-serifs feature clean modernist letter terminals.

questions.question: What CSS at-rule is used to load and declare custom web font files (.woff2, .woff, .ttf)?
questions.b: @web-font
questions.explanation: @font-face defines custom font family names and links them to local or remote font binaries.

questions.question: Which modern web font file format offers the highest compression efficiency and fastest web loading speeds?
questions.b: EOT (Embedded OpenType)
questions.explanation: WOFF2 uses Brotli compression, providing ~30% smaller file sizes than original WOFF.

questions.question: What does the 'font-display: swap;' descriptor in @font-face do?
questions.b: Instructs the browser to immediately display text using a system fallback font, then swap in the custom web font once downloaded (preventing FOIT - Flash of Invisible Text)
questions.explanation: font-display: swap eliminates blank text rendering delays on slow network connections.

questions.question: Which property sets the thickness/heaviness of font glyphs?
questions.b: font-thickness
questions.explanation: font-weight accepts keywords ('normal', 'bold') or numeric values from 100 to 900 (e.g. 400 = regular, 700 = bold).

questions.question: What does the numeric value 'font-weight: 700;' correspond to in standard typography?
questions.b: Regular / Normal
questions.explanation: 400 = Normal/Regular; 700 = Bold; 900 = Black.

questions.question: Which CSS property sets the vertical spacing distance between lines of text?
questions.b: line-height
questions.explanation: line-height controls vertical text baseline distance (e.g. line-height: 1.5).

questions.question: Why is using unitless numbers (e.g. 'line-height: 1.5;') preferred over fixed pixel values for line-height?
questions.a: Unitless line-height scales proportionally based on each descendant element's font size rather than locking children to a fixed parent height
questions.b: Pixel values are invalid
questions.explanation: Unitless line-height multiplies the current element's computed font-size dynamically.

questions.question: Which CSS property controls horizontal tracking spacing between individual characters?
questions.b: word-spacing
questions.explanation: letter-spacing expands or condenses spacing between character glyphs.

questions.question: What does 'text-transform: uppercase;' do?
questions.b: Transforms all text characters into capital UPPERCASE letters without altering the underlying HTML source code
questions.c: Capitalizes only the first letter of sentences
questions.explanation: text-transform alters case presentation (uppercase, lowercase, capitalize).

questions.question: What does 'text-transform: capitalize;' do?
questions.b: Capitalizes the First Letter of each word
questions.c: Capitalizes only the first word of a paragraph
questions.explanation: capitalize converts the initial letter of each word to uppercase.

questions.question: Which property controls text alignment within a block element?
questions.b: align-text
questions.explanation: text-align aligns text: left, right, center, or justify.

questions.question: What does 'text-align: justify;' do to paragraph text?
questions.b: Stretches and spaces out words so each line has equal width, aligning flush against both the left and right margins
questions.explanation: justify spaces lines to meet both left and right container edges simultaneously.

questions.question: What does 'text-decoration: underline;' do?
questions.b: Draws a solid underline beneath the text
questions.c: Draws a strike-through line across text
questions.explanation: text-decoration adds underlines, overlines, line-throughs, or removes link styling.

questions.question: How do you remove the default underline from HTML <a> hyperlink elements in CSS?
questions.b: link-style: no-underline;
questions.explanation: text-decoration: none strips default browser link underlines.

questions.question: Which combination of three CSS properties is required to truncate long overflowing single-line text with an ellipsis ('...')?
questions.a: white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;
questions.b: text-truncate: true; overflow: ellipsis; display: block;
questions.c: word-break: break-all; text-wrap: none; clip: auto;
questions.explanation: Single-line truncation strictly requires nowrap + hidden overflow + text-overflow: ellipsis.

questions.question: What does 'white-space: nowrap;' do to text?
questions.a: Collapses all whitespace to single spaces and prevents text from wrapping to the next line
questions.b: Wraps text at every comma
questions.c: Preserves all raw tabs and enter keys
questions.explanation: nowrap forces text into a continuous single horizontal line.

questions.question: What does 'word-break: break-word;' or 'overflow-wrap: break-word;' do?
questions.b: Allows unbroken lengthy words or URLs to break across lines to prevent container overflow
questions.explanation: break-word allows unbroken strings (like URLs) to break safely at container boundaries.

questions.question: What does 'text-shadow: 2px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.5);' do?
questions.b: Applies a drop shadow directly to letter glyphs (X-offset 2px, Y-offset 2px, Blur 4px, Color semi-transparent black)
questions.explanation: text-shadow creates glowing or drop-shadow effects on typography.

questions.question: What is the relative CSS unit 'em' relative to?
questions.b: The computed 'font-size' of the CURRENT element's direct parent (or the element itself for properties like padding)
questions.explanation: 1em equals the computed font-size of the parent context.

questions.question: What is the relative CSS unit 'rem' relative to?
questions.b: The Root element (<html>) font-size ONLY (Root EM)
questions.explanation: rem (Root EM) scales consistently against the root <html> font size (default 16px).

questions.question: If the root <html> font-size is 16px, how many pixels does '2.5rem' equal?
What does the CSS property 'font-style: italic;' do?
questions.b: Renders text using an italic / oblique cursive typeface design
questions.explanation: font-style toggles normal, italic, or oblique typographic variants.

questions.question: What is a 'Variable Font' in modern web typography?
questions.b: A single font file capable of smoothly interpolating across multiple design axes (weight, width, slant) continuously without loading separate bold/light files
questions.c: A font that changes color randomly
questions.explanation: Variable fonts contain continuous design variation axes in a single compact file.

questions.question: What does '-webkit-line-clamp: 3;' combined with 'display: -webkit-box;' accomplish?
questions.b: Truncates multi-line paragraph text after exactly 3 lines, adding an ellipsis at the cut-off point
questions.explanation: line-clamp truncates multi-line text gracefully across modern browsers.

questions.question: What does 'hyphens: auto;' do in CSS text formatting?
questions.b: Allows the browser to automatically insert hyphenation characters (-) when words break across line wraps based on language dictionary rules
questions.explanation: hyphens: auto hyphenates long wrapped words when the HTML lang attribute is declared.

questions.question: What does 'font-variant: small-caps;' render?
questions.b: Renders lowercase letters as smaller capitalized uppercase glyphs
questions.explanation: small-caps renders lowercase text as scaled capital letters.

questions.question: What does 'text-indent: 2rem;' do to a paragraph?
questions.a: Indents the very FIRST line of the paragraph inward by 2rem
questions.b: Indents all lines except the first
questions.c: Adds 2rem left margin to the entire block
questions.explanation: text-indent offsets the initial line of text in traditional editorial formatting.

questions.question: What is the primary visual behavior of a 'display: block;' element?
questions.b: Starts on a new line and stretches out horizontally to fill the full available width of its parent container
questions.explanation:
Block elements (
,

,

) generate line breaks and span 100% width by default.

questions.question: What is the visual behavior of a 'display: inline;' element?
questions.a: Takes up the whole width of the page
questions.b: Occupies only as much width as its content, sitting side-by-side on the same line with other inline elements without generating line breaks
questions.explanation: Inline elements (<span>, <a>, <strong>) flow horizontally within text lines.

questions.question: How does 'display: inline-block;' combine characteristics of both inline and block elements?
questions.a: It is identical to display: none
questions.b: It flows horizontally inline with text on the same line, but allows setting custom 'width', 'height', 'margin-top/bottom', and 'padding' like a block element
questions.explanation: inline-block elements align horizontally while respecting full box-model dimensional properties.

questions.question: What happens when an element is styled with 'display: none;'?
questions.a: The element becomes transparent but keeps its layout space
questions.b: The element is completely removed from the document layout flow, taking up zero space (invisible and non-interactive)
questions.c: The element is deleted from HTML DOM
questions.explanation: display: none collapses the element entirely from the visual flow.

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'display: none;' and 'visibility: hidden;'?
questions.b: 'display: none' removes the element from layout flow (0 space); 'visibility: hidden' hides the element visually while PRESERVING its exact layout space and dimensions on the page
questions.c: 'visibility: hidden' removes the element from DOM
questions.d: 'display: none' allows screen readers to read text
questions.explanation: visibility: hidden creates an invisible blank placeholder retaining original layout space.

questions.question: How does 'opacity: 0;' behave compared to 'visibility: hidden;' regarding user interactions (mouse clicks)?
questions.a: opacity: 0 elements can still receive mouse clicks and focus unless 'pointer-events: none;' is applied; visibility: hidden elements cannot receive clicks or focus
questions.b: opacity: 0 deletes the element
questions.d: Both behave identically in all aspects
questions.explanation: opacity: 0 elements remain active in the hit-test tree unless pointer-events are disabled.

questions.question: Which property disables all mouse and touch click interactions on an element?
questions.b: pointer-events: none;
questions.explanation: pointer-events: none passes mouse events through the element to underlying layers.

questions.question: What does 'user-select: none;' do on a web page?
questions.a: Prevents users from highlighting/selecting text on that element with cursor drags
questions.b: Disables keyboard typing
questions.explanation: user-select: none prevents accidental text selection on interactive UI buttons and cards.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes the mouse cursor icon when hovering over an element (e.g. to a hand pointer)?
questions.b: cursor: pointer;
questions.explanation: cursor: pointer displays the interactive hand cursor over clickable UI components.

questions.question: What does 'cursor: not-allowed;' display to the user?
questions.b: A circle with a slash (prohibition icon) indicating disabled or unavailable actions
questions.explanation: not-allowed signals disabled button or inactive form control states.

questions.question: What does 'display: contents;' do to an element container?
questions.b: Makes the container element itself disappear from the layout box tree, causing its direct children to act as direct children of the container's parent
questions.explanation: display: contents strips the container's box wrapper while preserving its child elements.

questions.question: Which CSS property allows users to resize a <div> element by dragging its bottom-right corner?
questions.a: resize: both; (requires overflow to be set to something other than visible)
questions.b: draggable: true;
questions.explanation: The 'resize' property (horizontal, vertical, both) enables UI resizing handles alongside overflow.

questions.question: What does 'clip-path: circle(50% at center);' do?
questions.b: Clips the rendered element into a circular shape, hiding everything outside the circular mask boundary
questions.d: Spins the element in a circle
questions.explanation: clip-path creates custom vector clipping geometries (circles, polygons, SVGs).

questions.question: What does 'clip-path: polygon(0 0, 100% 0, 100% 100%, 0 80%);' create?
questions.b: A custom quadrilateral with an angled/slanted bottom edge
questions.explanation: polygon() accepts coordinate pairs to produce angular geometrical masks.

questions.question: What is the default 'display' property value for an <a> or <span> element?
questions.b: inline
questions.explanation: Text-level semantic elements default to inline display.

questions.question:
What is the default 'display' value for
,
, and

elements?
questions.b: block
questions.explanation: Structural container elements default to block display.

questions.question: What does 'display: list-item;' generate on an element?
questions.b: A block box with an accompanying marker box (bullet point or numerical counter)
questions.explanation: list-item generates bullet marker boxes (as used natively on <li> tags).

questions.question: Which property controls the shape or style of list item bullets (e.g. disc, circle, square, none)?
questions.b: bullet-style
questions.explanation: list-style-type: none removes default bullet points from <ul> and <ol> lists.

questions.question: What does 'list-style-position: inside;' do?
questions.b: Places bullet markers INSIDE the content box of the list item, indenting text wrapping below the marker
questions.explanation: inside brings bullets into the inline text flow instead of outside the margin.

questions.question: What pseudo-element allows direct styling of the bullet marker or number on a list item?
questions.b: ::bullet
questions.explanation: ::marker targets list item bullets for custom color, font size, and content icons.

questions.question: What does 'display: table;' do to a regular <div>?
questions.a: Converts it to an SQL database
questions.b: Causes the element to behave visually like an HTML <table> element
questions.explanation: CSS table display values (table, table-row, table-cell) emulate tabular layout grids.

questions.question: What does 'display: none;' do to screen readers (accessibility)?
questions.a: Screen readers read the text normally
questions.b: Screen readers completely ignore and skip the hidden content because it is removed from the accessibility tree
questions.c: Screen readers read it in a whisper
questions.explanation: display: none hides content from both visual displays and assistive screen readers.

questions.question: How do you create an 'Accessible Visually Hidden' element (screen-reader only class)?
questions.b: Use a clip-path / 1px absolute clipping class that keeps text in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually from the screen
questions.explanation: sr-only utility classes visually clip elements to 1px while preserving accessibility tree announcements.

questions.question: What does 'visibility: collapse;' do when applied to table rows (<tr>)?
questions.b: Removes the row and frees up layout space without triggering re-calculation of table column widths (like display: none in tables)
questions.explanation: collapse optimizes dynamic table row hiding without layout jitter.

questions.question: What does 'aspect-ratio: 16 / 9;' do on a responsive video or card container?
questions.b: Maintains a consistent 16:9 proportional ratio between width and height automatically as dimensions change
questions.explanation: aspect-ratio prevents cumulative layout shifts (CLS) by reserving proportional space.

questions.question: What does 'object-fit: cover;' do when applied to an or
questions.a: Stretches the image to fill the box without preserving proportions
questions.b: Scales the media proportionally to fill the entire element content box, clipping excess edges to preserve aspect ratio
questions.explanation: object-fit: cover ensures images fill responsive container cards without distorting.

questions.question: What does 'object-fit: contain;' do?
questions.a: Scales media proportionally so the entire asset is visible inside the box without clipping, letterboxing if necessary
questions.b: Crops top and bottom
questions.explanation: object-fit: contain shows the complete uncropped media asset.

questions.question: Which property controls the alignment positioning of an within its box when using 'object-fit'?
questions.b: image-align
questions.explanation: object-position (e.g. center top) anchors the focal point of clipped media.

questions.question: What does the property 'accent-color: #3B82F6;' do in modern CSS?
questions.b: Styles native browser form controls (checkboxes, radio buttons, range sliders, progress bars) with the designated theme brand color
questions.explanation: accent-color themes built-in HTML form inputs with a single line of CSS.

questions.question: What does 'writing-mode: vertical-rl;' do in CSS?
questions.b: Lays out text vertically from top-to-bottom, with line progression from right-to-left (traditional East Asian typography)
questions.explanation: writing-mode enables vertical typography systems and artistic side-heading banners.

questions.question: What is the default value of the 'position' property for all HTML elements?
questions.b: static
questions.explanation: position: static is the natural document flow position where top/left/z-index properties have no effect.

questions.question: How does 'position: relative;' affect an element when top/left offsets are specified?
questions.a: Removes it from the document flow
questions.b: Offsets the element relative to its NORMAL static position without affecting the layout space of surrounding elements
questions.c: Locks it to the browser viewport
questions.explanation: relative shifts visual placement from its natural origin while keeping its original flow box intact.

questions.question: How does 'position: absolute;' position an element?
questions.a: Relative to the browser viewport only
questions.b: Relative to its closest positioned ancestor (an ancestor with position other than 'static'), removed from normal document flow
questions.explanation: absolute takes elements out of flow and positions them relative to the nearest positioned containing block.

questions.question: If an element has 'position: absolute;' and NONE of its ancestor parents have a position defined, what is it positioned relative to?
questions.b: The Initial Containing Block (the <html> root viewport)
questions.d: It fails to position and stays static
questions.explanation: In the absence of positioned ancestors, absolute elements anchor to the initial viewport root.

questions.question: How does 'position: fixed;' behave on a web page?
questions.b: Positions relative to the browser VIEWPORT and stays locked in the exact same place during page scrolling
questions.explanation: fixed pins UI bars (like sticky headers or floating action buttons) to the viewport coordinate system.

questions.question: How does 'position: sticky;' operate during scrolling?
questions.a: Acts as static by default, but becomes fixed once a specified scroll offset threshold (e.g. 'top: 0;') is reached within its scrolling container
questions.b: Sticks to the mouse cursor
questions.explanation: sticky toggles between relative and fixed positioning based on scroll threshold offsets.

questions.question: Why might 'position: sticky;' fail to stick when scrolling?
questions.a: Sticky elements cannot have background colors
questions.b: An ancestor container has 'overflow: hidden', 'overflow: auto', or 'overflow: scroll' which clips or intercepts the scroll boundary
questions.c: The element has a class name
questions.explanation: Ancestor overflow clipping breaks sticky scroll boundary detection.

questions.question: What does the 'z-index' property control in CSS?
questions.b: The vertical 3D stacking order of overlapping elements along the Z-axis (higher numbers render on top)
questions.explanation: z-index layers overlapping positioned elements along the perpendicular screen axis.

questions.question: Why does 'z-index: 9999;' sometimes fail to bring an element above an element with 'z-index: 1;'?
questions.b: The element is trapped inside a parent element that has established a separate, lower Stacking Context
questions.d: The element has a transparent background
questions.explanation: Stacking contexts isolate child z-indices; a child cannot escape its parent stacking context boundary.

questions.question: Which of the following actions creates a brand-new Stacking Context on an element?
questions.a: Setting opacity to less than 1 (e.g. opacity: 0.99;)
questions.b: Setting transform, filter, or backdrop-filter to a non-none value
questions.c: Setting position: fixed or position: sticky
questions.d: All of the above create a new stacking context
questions.explanation: Opacity < 1, transforms, filters, mix-blend-mode, and fixed positioning all spawn independent stacking contexts.

questions.question: What is the CSS shorthand property to set top, right, bottom, and left simultaneously?
questions.b: inset: 0;
questions.explanation: 'inset: 0;' is the modern shorthand equivalent to 'top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; left: 0;'.

questions.question: How do you center an absolute element perfectly in the middle of its container using transform?
questions.b: top: center; left: center;
questions.explanation: 50% top/left anchors the top-left corner at center, and translate(-50%, -50%) shifts back by half its own dimensions.

questions.question: What is the effect of 'top: 0; bottom: 0; margin: auto;' on an absolute element with a defined height?
questions.b: Perfectly centers the element vertically within its positioned parent container
questions.d: Draws a line at the top and bottom
questions.explanation: Constrained top/bottom 0 with margin: auto achieves vertical centering on absolute boxes.

questions.question: What does 'position: relative;' on a parent container achieve when wrapping an absolute child element?
questions.b: Establishes the parent as the containing reference coordinate block for the absolute child's top/left/right/bottom offsets
questions.explanation: position: relative creates the anchor coordinate frame for child absolute placements.

questions.question: Can an element with 'position: static;' use 'z-index'?
questions.a: Yes, static elements use z-index normally
questions.b: No, z-index only takes effect on positioned elements (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky) or flex/grid items
questions.c: Only if it has a border
questions.explanation: z-index is ignored on position: static elements in standard block flow.

questions.question: What happens when two positioned elements with the SAME z-index overlap?
questions.a: The element that appears LATER in the HTML DOM tree renders on top of the earlier one
questions.b: The first element in HTML always renders on top
questions.explanation: Equal z-index relies on DOM document source order to determine stacking superiority.

questions.question: What does 'inset-inline: 0;' do in CSS Logical Properties?
questions.b: Sets inline-start (left) and inline-end (right) offsets to 0 simultaneously
questions.explanation: inset-inline coordinates horizontal span boundaries across writing modes.

questions.question: What does 'inset-block: 0;' set in CSS Logical Properties?
questions.a: Sets block-start (top) and block-end (bottom) offsets to 0 simultaneously
questions.b: Left and right offsets to 0
questions.explanation: inset-block maps to vertical top and bottom offset constraints.

questions.question: What is the coordinate origin (0, 0) for a fixed positioned element?
questions.a: The top-left corner of the browser viewport
questions.b: The center of the webpage
questions.c: The top-left corner of the parent div
questions.explanation: Fixed positioning maps (0,0) to the top-left coordinate of the visible viewport screen.

questions.question: What happens if you apply 'transform: scale(1);' to an ancestor of a 'position: fixed;' element?
questions.b: The fixed child is no longer fixed to the viewport; it becomes contained and positioned relative to the transformed ancestor instead
questions.explanation: Transforms on ancestors trap fixed children, making the ancestor their containing block.

questions.question: What is a common UI pattern implemented using 'position: fixed; inset: 0;'?
questions.a: Full-screen modal backdrop / overlay dimming screen background
questions.b: Dropdown menu
questions.explanation: inset: 0 with fixed position creates full-viewport dialog overlays and lightboxes.

questions.question: What does 'pointer-events: auto;' do on a child inside a container with 'pointer-events: none;'?
questions.b: Re-enables click and touch events specifically for that child element while leaving the parent pass-through
questions.explanation: pointer-events: auto selectively re-activates hit testing on individual buttons inside pass-through overlays.

questions.question: Which value of 'position' removes an element from document flow while preserving its width unless specified?
questions.b: static
questions.explanation: absolute removes the element from flow, shrinking width to content unless explicit dimensions are declared.

questions.question: What is the stacking level order of native page components in a default Stacking Context?
questions.a: Background -> Borders -> Block descendants -> Floats -> Inline descendants -> Positioned descendants (z-index: 0) -> Positioned (z-index > 0)
questions.b: Text first, background last
questions.c: Positioned elements always render behind backgrounds
questions.explanation: The CSS 2.1 Stacking specification layers root backgrounds, blocks, floats, inlines, and positioned layers hierarchically.

questions.question: Can negative z-index values (e.g. 'z-index: -1;') be used in CSS?
questions.b: Yes, negative z-index places an element behind standard in-flow content and parent background within the stacking context
questions.explanation: z-index: -1 renders behind in-flow text and sibling elements.

questions.question: What happens when an absolute element specifies both 'left: 0;' and 'right: 0;' without a defined width?
questions.b: The element stretches horizontally to fill 100% of the containing parent width
questions.explanation: Dual opposing pin offsets (left: 0 + right: 0) force full horizontal stretch.

questions.question: What happens when an absolute element specifies both 'top: 0;' and 'bottom: 0;' without a defined height?
questions.a: It stretches vertically to span the entire height of its positioned containing parent
questions.b: Height becomes 0px
questions.explanation: Top and bottom 0 stretch element height to fill container bounds.

questions.question: Why is 'position: sticky;' preferred over JavaScript scroll event listeners for sticky navigation headers?
questions.a: CSS sticky is hardware-accelerated on the compositor thread, preventing scroll jank and layout reflows
questions.b: JavaScript cannot detect scroll positions
questions.explanation: Browser-native sticky positioning executes on compositor threads smoothly at 60/120 FPS.

questions.question: What is the effect of 'position: relative;' without any top/left/right/bottom declarations?
questions.a: No visual position change occurs, but it establishes a positioning context for absolute children and enables z-index control
questions.b: Element shifts 10px down
questions.explanation: A plain 'position: relative' creates a containing block and stacking hook without altering flow.

questions.question: How do you create a floating 'Badge' in the top-right corner of a button using CSS positioning?
questions.a: Button has 'position: relative;'; Badge has 'position: absolute; top: -5px; right: -5px;'
questions.b: Button has 'position: static;'; Badge has 'float: right;'
questions.c: Button has 'display: grid;'; Badge has 'align-self: top;'
questions.explanation: Relative parent container with absolute child offsets places notification badges perfectly.

questions.question: What does the Descendant Combinator (a space character 'div p') select in CSS?
questions.b:
All

elements that are descendants of a

, regardless of nesting depth (children, grandchildren, etc.)
questions.explanation: Space combinator selects all matching descendants anywhere within the ancestor subtree.

questions.question: What does the Child Combinator (greater-than sign 'ul > li') select?
questions.b: Only direct, first-generation child <li> elements immediately nested inside <ul>
questions.explanation: 'A > B' matches strictly direct children, ignoring deeper nested grandchild layers.

questions.question: What does the Adjacent Sibling Combinator (plus sign 'h2 + p') select?
questions.b:
The

element that immediately follows an

element as its direct next sibling with the same parent
questions.explanation: 'A + B' matches the single immediate next sibling element.

questions.question: What does the General Sibling Combinator (tilde sign 'h2 ~ p') select?
questions.b:
ALL

elements that follow an

element as siblings sharing the same parent (not just the first one)
questions.explanation: 'A ~ B' matches all subsequent sibling elements following A.

questions.question: Which attribute selector matches all <input> elements that have a 'required' attribute present?
questions.b: input.required
questions.explanation: [attribute] selects elements based on the existence of an attribute regardless of value.

questions.question: Which selector matches <input> elements where the type attribute is exactly 'email'?
questions.b: input.type-email
questions.explanation: [attribute='value'] matches exact attribute string equality.

questions.question: Which attribute selector matches links whose 'href' attribute STARTS with 'https://' (Prefix Match)?
questions.b: a[href*='https://']
questions.explanation: [attr^='val'] matches attributes beginning with the specified prefix string.

questions.question: Which attribute selector matches links whose 'href' attribute ENDS with '.pdf' (Suffix Match)?
questions.b: a[href^='.pdf']
questions.explanation: [attr$='val'] matches attributes terminating with the specified suffix string.

questions.question: Which attribute selector matches elements where the attribute CONTAINS a specific substring anywhere (Substring Match)?
questions.b: a[href^='download']
questions.explanation: [attr*='val'] matches substrings anywhere within the attribute string.

questions.question: What does the attribute selector '[class~=\'btn\']' match?
questions.b: Elements with a class attribute containing the exact word 'btn' in a whitespace-separated list
questions.d: Any class with the letters b-t-n
questions.explanation: [attr~='val'] matches whole words in whitespace-separated token lists.

questions.question: What does the attribute selector '[lang|=\'en\']' match?
questions.b: Elements with lang equal to 'en' OR starting with 'en-' (e.g. en-US, en-GB)
questions.explanation: [attr|='val'] matches hyphen-delimited language subcodes.

questions.question: How do you make an attribute selector Case-Insensitive in modern CSS (e.g. matching .pdf, .PDF, .Pdf)?
questions.a: Append the 'i' flag before the closing bracket (e.g. a[href$='.pdf' i])
questions.b: Use text-transform: lowercase
questions.explanation: The 'i' modifier forces case-insensitive attribute value matching.

questions.question: What does the 's' flag in an attribute selector (e.g. '[title*=\'Logo\' s]') enforce?
questions.b: Strict Case-Sensitive matching conforming to standard string case
questions.explanation: The 's' modifier forces case-sensitive attribute comparison.

questions.question: What does the selector 'nav > ul > li > a' select?
questions.b: Links that are direct children of list items, directly inside unordered lists, directly inside a <nav>
questions.explanation: Chained child combinators enforce rigid hierarchical nesting structure.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'p .highlight' and 'p.highlight'?
questions.b:
'p .highlight' selects descendants with class 'highlight' inside

; 'p.highlight' selects the

element itself that has class 'highlight'
questions.explanation: A space indicates a descendant combinator; lack of space indicates a compound selector on the same element.

questions.question: Which selector targets all disabled buttons in a form using attribute selectors?
questions.b: button.disabled
questions.explanation: button[disabled] selects buttons having the disabled attribute.

questions.question: How can you style external links opening in a new tab with an external icon indicator?
questions.b: a:external { icon: new-tab; }
questions.explanation: Attribute selector targeting target='_blank' coupled with ::after pseudo-element creates automatic link icons.

questions.question: What does the selector 'div[data-status=\'active\']' target?
questions.b: Div elements possessing a custom HTML5 data attribute 'data-status' whose value is exactly 'active'
questions.explanation: CSS attribute selectors seamlessly query custom data-* HTML5 attributes.

questions.question: What does the selector '*[hidden]' target in HTML5?
questions.b: Any element with the HTML5 boolean 'hidden' attribute declared
questions.explanation: Targets elements equipped with the native HTML5 hidden attribute.

questions.question: What does the compound selector 'input[type=\'checkbox\']:checked' select?
questions.b: Checkbox inputs that are currently in a checked / selected state
questions.explanation: Combines attribute selector with pseudo-class state for active checkboxes.

questions.question: What does the selector 'img:not([alt])' target in accessibility linting?
questions.b: Images that are missing the mandatory 'alt' accessibility description attribute entirely
questions.explanation: Detects inaccessible images lacking alt attributes.

questions.question: What does 'form :input' do in standard CSS?
questions.b: It is invalid syntax (':input' is a jQuery extension, not standard CSS; use 'form input, form select, form textarea' instead)
questions.explanation: :input is jQuery proprietary; standard CSS requires listing concrete element types.

questions.question: What does the selector 'section + section' target on a web page?
questions.b: Every <section> element EXCEPT the very first one (useful for adding top borders or margins between consecutive sections)
questions.explanation: The adjacent sibling pattern 'tag + tag' elegantly styles dividing margins between consecutive elements.

questions.question: What does the selector 'ol > li:first-child + li' select?
questions.b: The SECOND list item in an ordered list
questions.explanation: First-child plus adjacent sibling targets element #2.

questions.question: Can multiple attribute selectors be chained together on a single element (e.g. 'input[type=\'text\'][readonly]')?
questions.a: No, only one attribute selector is allowed
questions.b: Yes, and the element must satisfy ALL chained attribute conditions simultaneously
questions.explanation: Chained attribute selectors enforce multiple simultaneous attribute constraints.

questions.question: What does 'a[href^=\'mailto:\']' target in web styling?
questions.b: Email hyperlink mailto: URLs
questions.explanation: Targets email hyperlinks (mailto:).

questions.question: What does 'a[href^=\'tel:\']' target?
questions.b: Television links
questions.explanation: Targets mobile clickable telephone dialing URLs (tel:).

questions.question: What does 'input[type=\'radio\'] + label' commonly style in custom UI components?
questions.b: The text label directly following a radio button, used to create custom styled pill/toggle radio controls
questions.explanation: Classic accessible custom radio/checkbox design pattern using adjacent sibling labels.

questions.question: What does the selector ':root' target in CSS documents?
questions.b: The highest-level root element in the document tree (the <html> element in HTML documents), used for global custom property variables
questions.explanation: :root matches the top document node and holds global design tokens.

questions.question: What is the Specificity weight of the ':root' selector?
questions.b: (0, 0, 1, 0) Pseudo-class (same as a Class)
questions.explanation: :root is a pseudo-class with (0, 0, 1, 0) specificity, higher than the 'html' element selector.

questions.question: What is the key syntactic difference between a Pseudo-Class and a Pseudo-Element in CSS3?
questions.a: Pseudo-classes use a single colon ':' (e.g. :hover); Pseudo-elements use a double colon '::' (e.g. ::before)
questions.b: Pseudo-classes only style text
questions.explanation: CSS3 standardized single colon (:) for state pseudo-classes and double colon (::) for structural pseudo-elements.

questions.question: What does the ':hover' pseudo-class style?
questions.b: An element when the user positions the mouse pointer/cursor over it
questions.explanation: :hover applies visual feedback during mouseover.

questions.question: What does the ':active' pseudo-class style?
questions.b: An element during the exact moment it is being clicked or activated by the user (mouse button depressed)
questions.d: A form input with valid text
questions.explanation: :active represents the pressed / engaged interaction state.

questions.question: What does the ':focus' pseudo-class target?
questions.b: An interactive element (e.g. <input>, <button>, <a>) that currently has keyboard focus or input cursor focus
questions.explanation: :focus styles inputs and controls actively receiving keyboard/input focus.

questions.question: What does the modern ':focus-visible' pseudo-class do that ':focus' does not?
questions.a: Applies focus styling ONLY when focus is triggered via keyboard navigation (Tab key), avoiding unsightly focus rings on mouse clicks
questions.b: Hides the focus outline completely
questions.explanation: :focus-visible provides accessible keyboard focus rings without showing focus rings on mouse clicks.

questions.question: What does the ':focus-within' pseudo-class do on a container element (e.g. <form>)?
questions.b: Styles the parent container if the container itself OR ANY of its internal child elements currently has focus
questions.c: Prevents child inputs from receiving focus
questions.explanation: :focus-within activates on parent wrappers whenever any descendant gains focus.

questions.question: What is the required order of link pseudo-classes (the 'LVHA' rule) for styles to cascade correctly?
questions.b: :link -> :visited -> :hover -> :active (Love/Hate mnemonic)
questions.explanation: Link pseudo-classes must follow :link, :visited, :hover, :active (LVHA) to prevent rule shadowing.

questions.question: What does the ':visited' pseudo-class style?
questions.a: Links that the user has previously navigated to / visited in their browser history
questions.b: Bookmarked pages
questions.explanation: :visited styles previously clicked URL hyperlinks (restricted for privacy reasons).

questions.question: What does ':first-child' select?
questions.a: The first paragraph on a page
questions.b: An element that is the absolute FIRST child among all siblings within its parent container
questions.c: The first word in a text block
questions.explanation: :first-child matches an element that is the initial child of its parent.

questions.question: What does ':last-child' select?
questions.b: An element that is the absolute LAST child among siblings inside its parent container
questions.c: The last word in a paragraph
questions.explanation: :last-child matches an element that is the final sibling of its parent.

questions.question: What does the formula ':nth-child(2n)' or ':nth-child(even)' select in a table or list?
questions.b: All EVEN numbered child elements (2, 4, 6, 8, etc.) for striped row styling
questions.explanation: :nth-child(even) or (2n) selects even-indexed siblings for zebra-striping.

questions.question: What does ':nth-child(2n+1)' or ':nth-child(odd)' select?
questions.a: All ODD numbered child elements (1, 3, 5, 7, etc.)
questions.b: All even elements
questions.explanation: :nth-child(odd) selects odd-indexed siblings.

questions.question: What is the difference between ':nth-child()' and ':nth-of-type()'?
questions.b: ':nth-child()' counts ALL sibling elements regardless of tag type; ':nth-of-type()' counts ONLY siblings sharing the SAME HTML tag type
questions.explanation: :nth-of-type filters by tag name before applying numeric index counting.

questions.question: What does the ':only-child' pseudo-class target?
questions.b: An element that is the SOLE child of its parent (it has no sibling elements at all)
questions.c: The first child of the body
questions.explanation: :only-child targets elements without siblings.

questions.question: What does the ':not(selector)' negation pseudo-class do (e.g. 'button:not(.primary)')?
questions.b: Selects all buttons that DO NOT match the specified '.primary' class
questions.explanation: :not() matches elements failing the argument selector test.

questions.question: What does the powerful modern ':has()' relational pseudo-class (CSS Parent Selector) allow?
questions.a: Styles an element based on whether it CONTAINS or is followed by matching descendant/sibling elements (e.g. 'card:has(img)')
questions.b: Checks if a file exists on the server
questions.explanation: :has() enables styling parent elements conditionally based on child presence.

questions.question: What does ':empty' select in CSS?
questions.b: Elements that contain absolutely NO children and NO text nodes (not even whitespace)
questions.explanation: :empty matches elements devoid of child elements, text, or whitespace.

questions.question: What does ':disabled' and ':enabled' style?
questions.b: Interactive form inputs, buttons, and fieldsets in their disabled or enabled operational states
questions.explanation: :disabled targets inactive form controls.

questions.question: What does ':checked' match?
questions.b: Radio buttons, checkboxes, or <option> elements that are currently checked or selected
questions.explanation: :checked targets selected radio/checkbox form controls.

questions.question: What does the ':valid' and ':invalid' pseudo-classes evaluate on form inputs?
questions.b: Whether input values satisfy HTML5 form validation constraints (type, pattern, min, max, required)
questions.explanation: :valid/:invalid dynamically reflect HTML5 constraint validation states.

questions.question: Which mandatory CSS property MUST be declared for '::before' and '::after' pseudo-elements to render on the page?
questions.b: content: ''; (even if an empty string)
questions.explanation: Without declaring 'content', ::before and ::after generate no visual box.

questions.question: Where does '::before' insert generated decorative content relative to an element's HTML content?
questions.a: Before the element's opening tag outside the parent
questions.b: As the very FIRST child INSIDE the element, directly preceding its actual text content
questions.explanation: ::before generates content as the first inline child inside the element.

questions.question: Where does '::after' insert generated content?
questions.a: Outside the element after the closing tag
questions.b: As the very LAST child INSIDE the element, directly following its actual text content
questions.c: At the bottom of the webpage
questions.explanation: ::after generates content as the final child inside the element.

questions.question: What does the '::first-letter' pseudo-element style in editorial typography?
questions.a: The first word of a title
questions.b: The initial first character / letter of a block of text (used for Drop Caps styling)
questions.explanation: ::first-letter styles initial drop-cap characters in articles.

questions.question: What does the '::first-line' pseudo-element style?
questions.b: The entire first visual line of formatted text in a block element, dynamically adjusting as window width changes
questions.explanation: ::first-line styles the rendered top line of paragraph text.

questions.question: What does the '::placeholder' pseudo-element style?
questions.b: The temporary placeholder hint text displayed inside an empty <input> or <textarea>
questions.explanation: ::placeholder styles gray placeholder hint text inside form fields.

questions.question: What does the '::selection' pseudo-element style on a webpage?
questions.b: The highlighted text portion currently selected/dragged by the user with their mouse or cursor
questions.explanation: ::selection customizes background highlight and text color during user text selection.

questions.question: Can '::before' or '::after' pseudo-elements be applied to self-closing replaced elements like or ?
questions.b:
No, replaced elements (, ,
,
) have no internal child content tree and cannot host ::before or ::after pseudo-elements
questions.explanation: Replaced elements without child content trees cannot render pseudo-elements.

questions.question: What does ':target' pseudo-class select in single-page URL fragment navigation?
questions.b: The unique HTML element whose ID matches the current URL hash fragment (e.g. #section2)
questions.explanation: :target highlights the element targeted by the URL's #hash fragment identifier.

questions.question: What does ':autofill' (or ':-webkit-autofill') style in form inputs?
questions.a: Input fields that have been automatically populated by the browser's saved credentials/autofill manager
questions.b: Inputs filled by JavaScript
questions.explanation: :autofill targets fields populated by browser password/address managers.

questions.question: Which CSS declaration turns an element into a Flexbox Container?
questions.b: flex: 1;
questions.explanation: 'display: flex' activates the Flexbox formatting context on the container.

questions.question: What is the default 'flex-direction' in a flex container?
questions.b: row (horizontal left-to-right in LTR writing modes)
questions.explanation: The default flex-direction is 'row', aligning items horizontally.

questions.question: What happens when you set 'flex-direction: column;' on a flex container?
questions.a: Items arrange horizontally in a row
questions.b: The Main Axis becomes vertical; flex items stack vertically from top to bottom
questions.c: Items are placed in a 2D grid
questions.explanation: column rotates the Main Axis vertically.

questions.question: Which flex container property controls alignment of flex items along the MAIN AXIS?
questions.b: justify-content
questions.explanation: justify-content aligns items along the primary Main Axis.

questions.question: Which flex container property controls alignment of flex items along the CROSS AXIS (perpendicular axis)?
questions.b: align-items
questions.explanation: align-items aligns items across the perpendicular Cross Axis.

questions.question: What is the default value of 'align-items' in a flex container?
questions.b: center
questions.c: stretch (items stretch to fill the full cross-axis height of the container)
questions.explanation: stretch is the default align-items value.

questions.question: How do you perfectly center a child element both horizontally AND vertically using Flexbox on the parent?
questions.a: display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center;
questions.b: display: flex; align-content: middle;
questions.c: display: flex; text-align: center; vertical-align: middle;
questions.explanation: justify-content: center + align-items: center provides universal 2D centering.

questions.question: What does 'justify-content: space-between;' do to flex items?
questions.a: Packs items together at the start
questions.b: Distributes items evenly across the line, placing the first item flush against the start edge and the last item flush against the end edge
questions.c: Adds equal space around all items including outer ends
questions.explanation: space-between creates maximum separation with zero margin at extreme ends.

questions.question: What does 'justify-content: space-around;' do?
questions.a: Leaves no space at outer ends
questions.b: Distributes items with equal space around each item (resulting in end spaces being half the size of space between items)
questions.c: Pushes all items to the center
questions.explanation: space-around wraps each item in equal margins.

questions.question: What does 'justify-content: space-evenly;' do?
questions.a: Distributes items so that the space between any two items AND the space to the outer edges is exactly equal
questions.b: Stacks items on top of each other
questions.c: Forces all items to have equal widths
questions.explanation: space-evenly guarantees identical gap measurements everywhere.

questions.question: What is the default value of 'flex-wrap' on a flex container?
questions.b: nowrap (all flex items are forced onto a single line, shrinking if necessary to fit)
questions.explanation: nowrap is default; items compress into one row unless wrap is enabled.

questions.question: What happens when you declare 'flex-wrap: wrap;' on a flex container?
questions.a: Flex items will break onto multiple lines/rows as needed when space runs out
questions.b: Items become scrollable
questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap enables responsive multi-line wrapping.

questions.question: Which CSS property defines the gutter spacing between flex items without using margins?
questions.b: gap (or row-gap / column-gap)
questions.explanation: 'gap: 1rem;' provides clean gutter spacing between flex and grid items without outer edge margins.

questions.question: What does the flex item shorthand property 'flex: 1;' represent?
questions.b: flex-direction: 1;
questions.explanation: 'flex: 1;' expands the item to absorb all remaining free space equally.

questions.question: What does the 'flex-grow' property define on a flex item?
questions.b: The ability for a flex item to grow and expand proportionally to absorb remaining available positive free space in the container
questions.explanation: flex-grow distributes surplus container space proportionally.

questions.question: What is the default value of 'flex-grow' on a flex item?
questions.b: 0 (items do not grow beyond their natural content size unless specified)
questions.explanation: Default flex-grow is 0; items retain natural content size.

questions.question: What does the 'flex-shrink' property control?
questions.b: The ability for a flex item to shrink and compress proportionally when total item sizes exceed available container space
questions.explanation: flex-shrink handles negative space compression when containers are cramped.

questions.question: What is the default value of 'flex-shrink' on a flex item?
questions.b: 1 (items shrink automatically to prevent container overflow by default)
questions.explanation: Default flex-shrink is 1; items compress to avoid overflowing.

questions.question: How do you prevent a specific flex item (like an icon or avatar) from ever shrinking when space is tight?
questions.b: flex-grow: 0;
questions.explanation: flex-shrink: 0 locks the item at its defined size without compression.
