questions.question: What does 'flex-basis' define on a flex item?
questions.a: The maximum width of the item
questions.b: The initial default main size (width or height depending on direction) of the flex item before remaining free space is distributed
questions.explanation: flex-basis sets the baseline size before grow/shrink calculations occur.

questions.question: What does 'align-self' allow an INDIVIDUAL flex item to do?
questions.a: Override the container's 'align-items' cross-axis alignment value specifically for that single item
questions.b: Center itself horizontally
questions.explanation: align-self overrides the parent align-items rule on a per-item basis.

questions.question: What does the 'order' property do on flex items?
questions.b: Changes the visual rendering order of flex items without altering the underlying HTML DOM source code (default order is 0)
questions.explanation: order changes visual layout sequence without touching HTML structure.

questions.question: What is the effect of 'margin: auto;' on an individual flex item inside a flex container?
questions.b: It absorbs all remaining free space along that margin's direction (e.g. 'margin-left: auto;' pushes the item completely to the right edge)
questions.explanation: 'margin-left: auto' in flexbox is the gold-standard technique for pushing navbar links or action buttons to the far right.

questions.question: What does 'align-content' control in a flex container?
questions.b: Controls the cross-axis alignment of multiple WRAPPED lines/rows of flex items when there is extra vertical space (only applies when flex-wrap: wrap is active)
questions.c: Aligns items on a single line
questions.explanation: align-content aligns multiple wrapped flex lines across the cross axis.

questions.question: What does 'flex-direction: row-reverse;' do?
questions.b: Lays out flex items horizontally from right-to-left, placing the first DOM element at the far right
questions.d: Hides all items except the last
questions.explanation: row-reverse inverts horizontal sequence order.

questions.question: What is the shorthand property that combines 'flex-direction' and 'flex-wrap' simultaneously?
questions.b: flex-flow (e.g. flex-flow: row wrap;)
questions.explanation: flex-flow combines direction and wrapping (e.g. flex-flow: column wrap).

questions.question: What happens to the CSS 'float' and 'clear' properties on child elements when their parent becomes a flex container?
questions.b: Floats and clears are completely IGNORED on flex items; they have no effect in flex formatting contexts
questions.explanation: Flex formatting contexts supersede and disable traditional floats on flex items.

questions.question: What happens to vertical margin collapsing between adjacent child items inside a flex container?
questions.b: Vertical margin collapsing is completely DISABLED between flex items
questions.explanation: Flex items never collapse vertical margins.

questions.question: What does 'align-items: baseline;' align flex items to?
questions.a: The top edge of each item
questions.b: The typographical baseline of the first line of text inside each flex item, ensuring text across columns aligns perfectly
questions.explanation: baseline aligns unequal items by the font baseline of their first text line.

questions.question: What is 'Flexbox Holy Grail Layout' primarily composed of?
questions.a: A header, sticky footer, and a 3-column middle body section (nav, main content, sidebar) dynamically stretching to fill available viewport height
questions.b: A circular layout
questions.explanation: The Holy Grail layout uses flex columns and flex: 1 main sections to achieve responsive header/body/footer structures.

questions.question: What is the fundamental difference between CSS Flexbox and CSS Grid?
questions.a: Flexbox is 1-Dimensional (laying out items primarily along a single row OR column at a time); CSS Grid is 2-Dimensional (laying out rows AND columns simultaneously in a unified grid)
questions.b: Flexbox is newer than Grid
questions.explanation: Flexbox is 1D (content-first); Grid is 2D (layout-first system for simultaneous row and column orchestration).

questions.question: Which CSS property defines a Grid Container?
questions.b: grid-layout: on;
questions.explanation: 'display: grid' establishes a Grid formatting context.

questions.question: What does the fractional unit 'fr' represent in CSS Grid?
questions.b: A fraction of the available free space within the grid container (e.g. '1fr 2fr' divides space into 1/3 and 2/3 shares)
questions.explanation: The 'fr' unit allocates proportional shares of residual container space.

questions.question: What does 'grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);' create?
questions.b: 3 equal-width columns that each take up 1/3 of the available grid container width
questions.explanation: repeat(3, 1fr) produces three columns of identical 1fr fractional width.

questions.question: What does 'grid-template-columns: 200px 1fr 2fr;' configure?
questions.b: A fixed 200px first column, with the remaining width split between a 1-part second column and a 2-parts third column
questions.explanation: Mixes rigid fixed pixel units with flexible fractional distribution.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'minmax(150px, 1fr)' do in grid column sizing?
questions.b: Defines a dynamic size range: the column can shrink down to a minimum of 150px, but will expand up to 1fr if free space is available
questions.explanation: minmax(min, max) clamps track sizes between minimum and maximum bounds.

questions.question: What is the famous CSS Grid responsive column declaration that creates responsive auto-wrapping columns WITHOUT media queries?
questions.b: grid-columns: responsive;
questions.explanation: The 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(250px, 1fr))' recipe automatically fits as many 250px+ columns as viewport width allows without media queries.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'auto-fill' and 'auto-fit' in CSS Grid?
questions.b: 'auto-fill' creates empty grid tracks even if there are no items to fill them; 'auto-fit' collapses empty tracks to 0px, expanding existing items to fill the entire container row
questions.explanation: auto-fit stretches active items across empty trailing tracks; auto-fill reserves empty track slots.

questions.question: What does 'grid-template-areas' allow you to do in CSS Grid?
questions.a: Name specific visual regions of the grid layout using visual string ascii-art layouts (e.g. \'"header header" "sidebar main"\')
questions.b: Calculate physical room square footage
questions.explanation: grid-template-areas provides semantic template mapping for complete page layouts.

questions.question: How do you assign an individual child element to a named grid area defined in grid-template-areas?
questions.b: grid-area: header;
questions.explanation: grid-area connects child elements to matching named template area regions.

questions.question: What do Grid Line Numbers represent in CSS Grid placement?
questions.a: The count of items inside a cell
questions.b: The 1-based index numbers of the dividing grid track lines starting from the start edge (1, 2, 3... -1 for the end line)
questions.d: The pixel width of grid borders
questions.explanation: Grid lines delineate track boundaries, numbered 1..N (or -1 for reverse end).

questions.question: What does 'grid-column: 1 / 3;' do to a grid item?
questions.b: Causes the grid item to span horizontally from grid line 1 up to (but not including) grid line 3 (spanning 2 columns)
questions.c: Positions the item on row 1, column 3
questions.explanation: Line-based placement 'start / end' specifies horizontal span boundaries.

questions.question: What does 'grid-column: span 2;' mean?
questions.b: Causes the item to span across 2 adjacent columns starting from its current auto-placed position
questions.explanation: The span keyword widens a cell across N columns relative to current placement.

questions.question: What does 'grid-column: 1 / -1;' do in a grid layout?
questions.a: Causes the grid item to span across the ENTIRE full width of the grid from the very first line (1) to the very last line (-1)
questions.b: Deletes column 1
questions.explanation: '1 / -1' spans items across the complete width of explicit grid templates.

questions.question: What does 'grid-row: span 3;' do to a grid item?
questions.a: Spans the item vertically across 3 consecutive rows
questions.b: Creates 3 new rows
questions.explanation: Spans item vertically downward across 3 row tracks.

questions.question: What is the difference between the 'Explicit Grid' and the 'Implicit Grid'?
questions.a: Explicit grid is defined in CSS; implicit grid is created automatically by the browser when items overflow explicit row/column tracks
questions.b: Explicit grid is 3D; implicit grid is 2D
questions.c: Explicit grid uses pixels; implicit grid uses rem
questions.d: There is no implicit grid in CSS
questions.explanation: Implicit grids auto-generate new rows/columns to accommodate extra DOM nodes.

questions.question: Which property defines the automatic default height of rows created in the Implicit Grid?
questions.b: grid-implicit-height
questions.explanation: grid-auto-rows governs the dimension of automatically created implicit rows.

questions.question: Which property defines whether auto-placed items fill into new rows or new columns?
questions.b: grid-direction
questions.explanation: grid-auto-flow controls placement direction (row, column, row dense).

questions.question: What does 'grid-auto-flow: dense;' do in an image gallery or masonry-style layout?
questions.b: Instructs the auto-placement algorithm to backfill earlier empty holes/gaps in the grid if smaller items appear later in the DOM
questions.explanation: dense packs layouts tightly by filling vacant grid holes out-of-order.

questions.question: What does the shorthand property 'place-items: center;' do on a grid container?
questions.b: Combines 'align-items: center;' and 'justify-items: center;' to perfectly center all grid items inside their respective grid cells in both axes
questions.c: Centers the grid on the screen
questions.explanation: 'place-items: center' provides instant 2D grid cell centering.

questions.question: What does 'place-content: center;' do on a grid container when total grid track size is smaller than the container?
questions.a: Centers the entire grid system itself (all tracks collectively) within the outer container
questions.b: Centers text inside paragraphs
questions.explanation: place-content aligns the entire track collection within container boundaries.

questions.question: What does 'justify-self: end;' do on an individual grid item?
questions.a: Pushes the item to the right edge of its own individual grid cell along the inline axis
questions.b: Moves the item to the last row
questions.explanation: justify-self overrides cell-level inline alignment for a single item.

questions.question: What does 'align-self: start;' do on an individual grid item?
questions.a: Aligns the item to the top edge of its own grid cell along the block/vertical axis
questions.b: Moves item to row 1
questions.explanation: align-self overrides vertical cell alignment for that specific item.

questions.question: Can grid items intentionally overlap each other in CSS Grid?
questions.a: No, grid items are strictly prohibited from overlapping
questions.b: Yes, by assigning multiple items to identical grid line coordinates or grid areas, layering them with z-index
questions.explanation: CSS Grid natively supports deliberate overlapping layers (e.g. hero image with text overlay card).

questions.question: What is 'CSS Subgrid' ('grid-template-columns: subgrid;')?
questions.b: A modern feature allowing a nested child grid to adopt and inherit the exact row/column track definitions of its parent grid, aligning items across cards perfectly
questions.explanation: Subgrid synchronizes nested child alignment with parent track coordinate grids.

questions.question: What does the declaration 'grid-template-columns: 100px auto 1fr;' create?
questions.b: Column 1 is fixed at 100px; Column 2 sizes to its largest content ('auto'); Column 3 absorbs all remaining free space ('1fr')
questions.explanation: Combines fixed (100px), intrinsic content (auto), and flexible (1fr) column sizing.

questions.question: How do you define a 16px gutter spacing between both rows and columns in CSS Grid?
questions.b: grid-margin: 16px;
questions.explanation: 'gap: 16px;' establishes uniform gutter alleys across all grid rows and columns.

questions.question: What does 'row-gap: 20px; column-gap: 10px;' configure?
questions.a: Vertical gap between rows is 20px; Horizontal gap between columns is 10px
questions.b: Rows 10px, Columns 20px
questions.explanation: Separate row and column gap dimensions.

questions.question: Can CSS Grid be used together with CSS Flexbox on the same web page?
questions.a: No, using both crashes the CSS parser
questions.b: Yes! Best practice is using CSS Grid for the macro 2D page layout, and Flexbox for micro 1D component alignments (navbars, card actions, tags)
questions.c: Only if declared in separate files
questions.d: Grid is deprecated in favor of Flexbox
questions.explanation: Modern web design combines Grid for macro page scaffolds with Flexbox for micro UI components.

questions.question: What does the '.' (period) token represent inside a 'grid-template-areas' declaration (e.g. \'"header header" ". main"\')?
questions.b: An empty, unnamed cell slot in the grid template where no item is placed
questions.explanation: A dot (.) in template areas creates deliberate empty spacer cells in the grid map.

questions.question: Which CSS property applies 2D or 3D geometrical transformation matrices to an element?
questions.b: transform
questions.explanation: The 'transform' property rotates, scales, skews, or translates elements.

questions.question: What does 'transform: translate(50px, 100px);' do to an element?
questions.b: Moves the element 50px to the right along the X-axis and 100px down along the Y-axis without affecting surrounding layout flow
questions.explanation: translate(X, Y) shifts visual position without triggering layout reflow.

questions.question: What does 'transform: rotate(45deg);' do?
questions.a: Rotates the element 45 degrees clockwise around its transform origin
questions.b: Rotates the element 45 degrees counter-clockwise
questions.c: Bends the text at a 45 degree angle
questions.d: Crops the element into a diamond
questions.explanation: rotate(Ndeg) spins elements clockwise around the anchor point.

questions.question: What does 'transform: scale(1.5);' do?
questions.a: Enlarges the element by 150% (1.5 times its original size) in both width and height
questions.b: Shrinks the element by 50%
questions.explanation: scale(factor) multiplies element dimensions proportionally.

questions.question: What does 'transform: scaleX(-1);' achieve on an image or element?
questions.b: Flips / mirrors the element horizontally along the vertical axis (Horizontal Mirror effect)
questions.explanation: Negative scaleX values flip elements horizontally.

questions.question: What does 'transform: scaleY(-1);' achieve?
questions.a: Flips / mirrors the element vertically upside-down (Vertical Mirror effect)
questions.b: Shrinks height to 0
questions.explanation: scaleY(-1) flips an element upside down vertically.

questions.question: What does 'transform: skew(10deg, 20deg);' do to an element?
questions.a: Distorts and slants the element along the X and Y axes by the specified degree angles (Shear transformation)
questions.b: Rotates the element
questions.explanation: skew(Xdeg, Ydeg) produces shear slant distortions.

questions.question: What is the default point of origin for CSS transformations ('transform-origin')?
questions.b: 50% 50% (The exact center of the element)
questions.explanation: The default transform-origin is '50% 50%' (the element's geometric center).

questions.question: How do you rotate an element around its Top-Left corner rather than its center?
questions.b: transform-anchor: top-left;
questions.explanation: transform-origin: top left pivots transformations from the top-left coordinate.

questions.question: How do you chain multiple transform functions on a single element (e.g. translate AND rotate)?
questions.a: Declare transform multiple times on separate lines
questions.b: List each transform function separated by a space in a single declaration: 'transform: translate(20px, 0) rotate(45deg) scale(1.2);'
questions.explanation: Space-separated function chains execute sequentially from right to left.

questions.question: Why does the order of transform functions matter in 'transform: rotate(45deg) translate(100px, 0);' vs 'transform: translate(100px, 0) rotate(45deg);'?
questions.a: It does not matter in CSS
questions.b: Transformations modify the coordinate system itself; rotating first causes subsequent translations to move along the newly tilted 45-degree axis
questions.explanation: Matrix transformations are non-commutative; rotation alters directional axes for subsequent translations.

questions.question: What CSS property is required on a parent container to enable 3D perspective depth for transformed 3D child elements?
questions.b: perspective: 800px; (or transform: perspective(800px);)
questions.explanation: perspective determines the virtual distance between the viewer and the z=0 plane.

questions.question: What does 'transform: rotateY(180deg);' do to a card in a 3D flipping animation?
questions.a: Spins the card vertically upside down
questions.b: Rotates the card horizontally around its vertical Y-axis by 180 degrees, showing the back of the card
questions.explanation: rotateY(180deg) rotates objects around the vertical spine for card-flip UI effects.

questions.question: What does 'transform: rotateX(180deg);' do?
questions.a: Flips the element vertically around its horizontal X-axis
questions.b: Flips the element horizontally
questions.explanation: rotateX(180deg) flips cards top-to-bottom around the horizontal axis.

questions.question: What does 'backface-visibility: hidden;' do in a 3D card flip component?
questions.a: Hides the front face when looking from behind
questions.b: Hides the back side of the element when it is rotated to face away from the viewer (showing the underlying back card face instead)
questions.explanation: backface-visibility: hidden is critical for 2-sided 3D flipping card components.

questions.question: What does 'transform-style: preserve-3d;' do on a 3D parent container?
questions.a: Flattens all child elements into a single 2D plane
questions.b: Instructs the browser to render child elements in their shared true 3D coordinate space rather than flattening them to 2D
questions.explanation: preserve-3d maintains true 3D spatial relationships for nested child elements.

questions.question: What does 'transform: translateZ(100px);' do in a 3D perspective context?
questions.a: Moves the element 100px to the right
questions.b: Pushes the element 100px closer toward the viewer along the Z-axis (making it appear physically closer and larger in perspective)
questions.c: Pushes the element backward into the screen
questions.explanation: translateZ moves elements forward/backward along the perpendicular depth axis.

questions.question: Why are CSS Transforms and Opacity animations preferred over animating 'top', 'left', 'width', or 'height'?
questions.a: Transforms and opacity are executed on the GPU compositor thread without triggering layout reflows or repaints, ensuring silky 60/120 FPS performance
questions.b: Top and left are deprecated in CSS3
questions.d: Transforms work on older browsers only
questions.explanation: Compositor-only properties (transform, opacity) bypass CPU layout reflow bottlenecks.

questions.question: What does 'perspective-origin: center top;' configure in a 3D scene?
questions.a: Sets the position of the 3D model
questions.b: Sets the viewer's virtual eye-level / vanishing point angle (looking down at the 3D scene from above center)
questions.explanation: perspective-origin positions the vanishing point coordinates of the 3D camera view.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'matrix3d()' accept?
questions.b: A 4x4 homogeneous transformation matrix of 16 numerical values for complex 3D transformations
questions.explanation: matrix3d() takes 16 values defining affine 3D matrix transformations.

questions.question: What does 'transform: translate3d(x, y, z);' do?
questions.a: Moves the element across all three X, Y, and Z dimensional spatial coordinates simultaneously
questions.b: Creates 3 duplicate copies
questions.explanation: translate3d applies hardware-accelerated 3D vector translation.

questions.question: In modern CSS, can individual transform properties (e.g. 'translate: 50px 100px;', 'rotate: 45deg;', 'scale: 1.2;') be declared independently?
questions.a: No, you must always use the transform shorthand
questions.b: Yes! Modern CSS supports standalone 'translate', 'rotate', and 'scale' properties that can be animated independently without overwriting each other
questions.explanation: Independent transform properties allow modular animation without transform function collisions.

questions.question: What does 'rotate: x 45deg;' do when using independent transform properties?
questions.a: Rotates 45 degrees around the X-axis in 3D space
questions.b: Rotates along the 2D plane
questions.explanation: Independent rotate properties accept axis qualifiers (e.g. rotate: y 90deg).

questions.question: What does 'scale: 2 0.5;' do when using independent transform properties?
questions.a: Scales width by 2x and height by 0.5x independently
questions.b: Scales by 2.5x
questions.explanation: Independent scale property accepts X and Y factors.

questions.question: What does 'transform: matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 50, 100);' represent in 2D?
questions.a: A translation of 50px on X and 100px on Y with no scaling or rotation
questions.b: A rotation of 50 degrees
questions.explanation: Standard 2D affine matrix(a, b, c, d, tx, ty) where tx=50 and ty=100.

questions.question: What does 'will-change: transform;' do when applied before an animation?
questions.b: Hints to the browser's rendering engine to promote the element to its own dedicated GPU compositor layer in advance, optimizing performance
questions.explanation: will-change advises browser rendering engines to prepare dedicated compositor layers.

questions.question: Why should 'will-change' NOT be applied indiscriminately to all elements (* { will-change: transform; })?
questions.b: Promoting excessive elements to GPU layers consumes massive VRAM and degrades browser memory performance
questions.explanation: Overusing will-change triggers high VRAM consumption and GPU layer thrashing.

questions.question: What does 'transform: translate(-50%, -50%);' use as its percentage reference basis?
questions.a: The parent container's width and height
questions.b: The element's OWN computed width and height
questions.explanation: Transform percentage coordinates are calculated relative to the element's own dimensions.

questions.question: What visual effect does 'transform: perspective(500px) rotateX(25deg);' create on a flat container?
questions.a: A 3D tilted 'Star Wars crawl' or receding billboard plane effect
questions.b: A flat 2D rectangle
questions.explanation: Transforms with perspective tilting create receding 3D floor/plane visual angles.

questions.question: Can an inline element (like standard <span>) be transformed with 'transform' without changing its display?
questions.b: No, transform has no effect on pure inline elements; the element must be set to 'inline-block', 'block', 'flex', or 'grid' to transform
questions.explanation: CSS transforms only apply to transformable elements (block, inline-block, flex/grid items, etc.).

questions.question: What is the primary function of the CSS 'transition' property?
questions.a: To animate elements continuously in an infinite loop
questions.b: To provide smooth, gradual visual interpolations between two CSS property states (e.g. normal state to :hover state)
questions.c: To redirect users to another webpage
questions.explanation: Transitions smoothly interpolate property state changes over a specified duration.

questions.question: What are the four sub-properties of the 'transition' shorthand property in CSS?
questions.b: transition: name iteration count direction;
questions.explanation: transition shorthand syntax: property, duration, timing-function, delay (e.g. all 0.3s ease 0.1s).

questions.question: Which CSS property specifies how long a transition should take to complete?
questions.b: transition-duration (e.g. 0.3s or 300ms)
questions.explanation: transition-duration specifies elapsed time in seconds (s) or milliseconds (ms).

questions.question: What does the 'transition-timing-function' control during an animation?
questions.b: The acceleration curve / pacing of the transition over time (e.g. linear, ease-in, ease-out, cubic-bezier)
questions.explanation: Timing functions modulate velocity curves (accelerating, decelerating, springing).

questions.question: What is the characteristic behavior of the 'ease-in-out' timing function?
questions.b: Starts slowly, accelerates in the middle, and decelerates slowly at the end
questions.explanation: ease-in-out produces natural smooth acceleration and deceleration.

questions.question: What does the 'linear' timing function do?
questions.b: Maintains an exact constant velocity from start to finish without acceleration or deceleration
questions.explanation: linear progresses at a steady uniform rate across the animation lifespan.

questions.question: What does the 'cubic-bezier(x1, y1, x2, y2)' function allow in CSS animations?
questions.b: Defining custom bezier velocity curves (including realistic spring, overshoot, and bounce physics)
questions.explanation: cubic-bezier defines custom 4-point Bézier velocity curves.

questions.question: What does the 'steps(5, end)' timing function do in a CSS animation?
questions.b: Divides the transition into 5 discrete, instantaneous jumps/frames (used for sprite-sheet animations and retro typewriter text effects)
questions.explanation: steps() segments animations into stepped frame intervals (sprite sheets).

questions.question: Which CSS at-rule is used to define complex, multi-stage custom CSS animations?
questions.b: @keyframes (e.g. @keyframes slideIn { 0% {} 100% {} })
questions.explanation: @keyframes creates named animation sequences with percentage step waypoints.

questions.question: What do 'from' and 'to' represent inside a @keyframes rule?
questions.b: Syntactic aliases for 0% (start) and 100% (completion)
questions.explanation: 'from' is 0% and 'to' is 100% in keyframe rule syntax.

questions.question: Which property binds a @keyframes animation name to an HTML element?
questions.b: keyframes-bind: pulse;
questions.explanation: animation-name connects the element to the matching @keyframes definition.

questions.question: How do you make a CSS animation loop infinitely without stopping?
questions.b: animation-loop: true;
questions.explanation: animation-iteration-count: infinite runs the animation continuously.

questions.question: What does 'animation-direction: alternate;' do to an animation loop?
questions.a: Plays the animation in reverse only
questions.b: Plays the animation forwards on odd iterations and backwards in reverse on even iterations (ping-pong effect)
questions.explanation: alternate reverses playback direction on alternating iteration cycles.

questions.question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: forwards;' ensure when an animation completes?
questions.a: The element resets to its original pre-animation styles immediately
questions.b: The element retains the exact computed style values defined in the LAST keyframe (100%) after the animation finishes
questions.d: The element is deleted from DOM
questions.explanation: forwards preserves final keyframe styles permanently after animation ends.

questions.question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: backwards;' do?
questions.b: Applies the styles of the FIRST keyframe (0%) immediately during the animation-delay period before the animation actually starts playing
questions.explanation: backwards applies 0% styles during initial delay wait intervals.

questions.question: What does 'animation-fill-mode: both;' do?
questions.a: Applies rules for both forwards AND backwards fill modes
questions.b: Plays forwards and backwards simultaneously
questions.explanation: 'both' combines initial delay styling (backwards) with final persistence (forwards).

questions.question: Which property can pause and resume a running CSS animation on hover or click?
questions.b: animation-play-state: paused; (or animation-play-state: running;)
questions.explanation: animation-play-state: paused freezes running animations in place.

questions.question: Why is 'transition: all 0.3s;' generally discouraged in performance-critical production code?
questions.b: It forces the browser to watch and interpolate every single property (including costly layout/paint properties like width/box-shadow), causing frame drops
questions.d: It is not supported in Chrome
questions.explanation: Explicitly listing properties (e.g. transition: transform 0.2s, opacity 0.2s) prevents unneeded paint recalculations.

questions.question: What is the CSS media query used to detect if a user has enabled reduced motion preferences in their operating system?
questions.b: @media (no-animations: true)
questions.explanation: prefers-reduced-motion respects vestibular disorders by disabling aggressive UI animations.

questions.question: How do you implement accessible reduced-motion rules in modern CSS?
questions.b: Delete all animations manually
questions.c: Use JavaScript to slow down the CPU
questions.explanation: Overriding animation/transition durations to near-zero provides comprehensive motion accessibility.

questions.question: Can CSS transitions animate between 'height: 0;' and 'height: auto;' smoothly in standard CSS2/CSS3?
questions.a: Yes, height: auto transitions smoothly by default
questions.b: No, standard CSS transitions cannot interpolate between a fixed length and the intrinsic keyword 'auto' (modern CSS solves this with 'interpolate-size' or Grid 0fr->1fr)
questions.explanation: Traditional CSS cannot interpolate to 'auto'; modern CSS uses Grid (0fr to 1fr) or interpolate-size: allow-keywords.

questions.question: How can you smoothly transition an accordion collapse from 0 to full height using CSS Grid?
questions.a: grid-template-rows: 0fr; transitioning to grid-template-rows: 1fr; (with min-height: 0 on child)
questions.b: display: none transitioning to display: block
questions.explanation: Transitioning grid-template-rows from 0fr to 1fr achieves smooth accordion expanding without fixed pixel heights.

questions.question: What does 'transition-delay: 0.5s;' do?
questions.b: Waits for 0.5 seconds AFTER the trigger event before starting the transition interpolation
questions.explanation: transition-delay introduces an idle waiting interval before animation execution begins.

questions.question: What happens if a negative delay is assigned to an animation (e.g. 'animation-delay: -2s;')?
questions.a: The animation is delayed by 2 seconds
questions.b: The animation starts IMMEDIATELY as if it had already been playing for 2 seconds (starts mid-sequence)
questions.explanation: Negative delays skip forward into the animation cycle, starting playback mid-timeline.

questions.question: What is a 'CSS Pulse / Heartbeat' animation pattern typically composed of?
questions.a: A @keyframes sequence that alternates 'transform: scale(1);' to 'transform: scale(1.08);' continuously with 'animation-direction: alternate;'
questions.b: Changing background colors between red and green
questions.explanation: Subtle scale keyframe loops create engaging pulse badges and call-to-action indicators.

questions.question: What is a 'CSS Shimmer / Skeleton Loading' animation composed of?
questions.b: A moving linear-gradient background highlighting across placeholder cards from left to right using @keyframes background-position
questions.explanation: Shimmer skeletons animate gradient positions across muted grey UI card mockups.

questions.question: What does 'animation-direction: reverse;' do?
questions.a: Plays the animation from 100% (to) back to 0% (from) in reverse order
questions.b: Flips the element upside down
questions.explanation: reverse inverts keyframe timeline progression.

questions.question: Can multiple animations be assigned to a single element simultaneously in CSS?
questions.a: No, only one animation is allowed per element
questions.b: Yes, by separating animation names and properties with commas (e.g. 'animation: fadeIn 0.5s ease, slideUp 0.5s ease;')
questions.explanation: Comma-separated animation lists composite multiple concurrent keyframe sequences.

questions.question: What is the CSS 'view-transition' API in modern web development?
questions.b: A modern browser API allowing smooth visual animated transitions between different DOM states or full multi-page document navigations (MPAs)
questions.explanation: View Transitions provide native app-like animated page transitions across DOM updates and navigation.

questions.question: What does '@keyframes spin { to { transform: rotate(360deg); } }' combined with 'animation: spin 1s linear infinite;' create?
questions.b: A bouncing ball
questions.explanation: The canonical CSS loading spinner animation.

questions.question: What is the mandatory HTML meta viewport tag required for responsive web design?
questions.b: <meta name=\'screen\' content=\'mobile\'>
questions.explanation: The viewport meta tag aligns page layout width to physical device screen width and establishes 1:1 scale.

questions.question: What does the 'Mobile-First' responsive design approach mean?
questions.a: Building the website only for mobile phones and ignoring desktops
questions.b: Writing base CSS styles for mobile/small screens first, then using '@media (min-width: ...)' to progressively enhance layout for larger desktop screens
questions.c: Designing desktop first and stripping features on mobile
questions.explanation: Mobile-first begins with mobile base styles, adding complexity upward via min-width media queries.

questions.question: What does the media query '@media (min-width: 768px)' target?
questions.b: Screens that are 768 pixels wide OR WIDER (tablets, laptops, desktops)
questions.explanation: min-width activates styles at or above the declared breakpoint.

questions.question: What does the media query '@media (max-width: 767px)' target?
questions.a: Screens that are 767 pixels wide OR SMALLER (mobile phones)
questions.b: Screens wider than 767px
questions.explanation: max-width targets viewports up to the declared upper ceiling.

questions.question: What is the modern CSS Media Query Range Syntax supported in modern browsers?
questions.b: @media (between: 768px and 1024px)
questions.explanation: Modern CSS supports mathematical comparison operators (e.g. width >= 768px and width <= 1024px).

questions.question: What does the media query '@media (orientation: landscape)' detect?
questions.a: Devices held in a horizontal orientation where viewport width is greater than height
questions.b: Vertical mobile phone holding
questions.explanation: landscape triggers when width > height; portrait triggers when height > width.

questions.question: What does the media query '@media (orientation: portrait)' detect?
questions.a: Devices held vertically where viewport height is greater than width
questions.b: Horizontal tablet holding
questions.explanation: portrait matches viewports where height >= width.

questions.question: What does '@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)' enable in CSS?
questions.b: Detects if the user has enabled Dark Mode in their operating system / browser preferences, allowing automatic dark theme styling
questions.explanation: prefers-color-scheme detects system light/dark theme settings for responsive themes.

questions.question: What does '@media print' target?
questions.b: Print preview modes and physical printer outputs (used to hide navigation bars, banners, and adjust margins for printing)
questions.explanation: @media print creates clean, ink-friendly layouts for PDF exporting and printing.

questions.question: What does the CSS viewport unit '100vw' represent?
questions.b: 100% of the entire Viewport Width (including scrollbar width if present)
questions.explanation: 1vw equals 1% of the total browser viewport width.

questions.question: What does the CSS viewport unit '100vh' represent?
questions.b: 100 virtual horizontal pixels
questions.explanation: 1vh equals 1% of the browser viewport height.

questions.question: Why do the modern dynamic viewport units '100dvh', '100svh', and '100lvh' exist for mobile browsers?
questions.a: To handle mobile browser dynamic address bars / toolbars showing and hiding without causing jumpy layout shifts (Dynamic, Small, Large Viewport Height)
questions.b: To calculate device battery percentage
questions.explanation: dvh/svh/lvh adapt gracefully to mobile browser collapsible URL address bars.

questions.question: What does 'vmin' represent in CSS viewport units?
questions.a: 1% of the SMALLEST of either viewport width or viewport height (whichever is smaller)
questions.b: 1% of viewport width
questions.explanation: vmin picks the smaller viewport dimension; vmax picks the larger dimension.

questions.question: What does 'vmax' represent?
questions.a: 1% of the LARGEST of either viewport width or viewport height (whichever is larger)
questions.b: 100% of the screen
questions.explanation: vmax resolves against whichever viewport dimension is currently larger.

questions.question: What does the CSS mathematical function 'calc()' allow you to do?
questions.b: Perform dynamic mathematical calculations mixing different CSS units (e.g. 'width: calc(100% - 40px);')
questions.explanation: calc() evaluates algebraic expressions mixing percentages, pixels, rem, and viewport units.

questions.question: Why is whitespace around '+' and '-' operators strictly MANDATORY inside 'calc()' (e.g. 'calc(100% - 20px)')?
questions.b: Without spaces, a minus sign (like '-20px') is parsed as a negative number literal rather than a subtraction operator, causing a syntax error
questions.explanation: calc() requires spaces around + and - to disambiguate subtraction from negative value units.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'min(50vw, 500px)' evaluate to?
questions.b: Selects the SMALLEST computed value among the listed options (effectively acting as a maximum width ceiling)
questions.explanation: min() picks the smallest value in the argument list.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'max(10vw, 200px)' evaluate to?
questions.b: Selects the LARGEST computed value among the listed options (effectively acting as a minimum size floor)
questions.explanation: max() selects the largest value, enforcing a minimum dimensional floor.

questions.question: What does the CSS function 'clamp(min, preferred, max)' do (e.g. 'font-size: clamp(1rem, 2.5vw, 2rem);')?
questions.a: Clamps the value so it scales fluidly with the preferred value, but NEVER shrinks below 'min' and NEVER grows above 'max' (Fluid Typography)
questions.b: Locks the font size permanently
questions.explanation: clamp() implements fluid responsive typography without writing dozens of media query breakpoints.

questions.question: What is 'Fluid Typography' in modern responsive design?
questions.a: Fonts that change color like water
questions.b: Text that smoothly and continuously scales in size proportionally with the viewport width (using clamp and vw) rather than jumping at discrete media query breakpoints
questions.explanation: Fluid typography eliminates discrete breakpoint jumps for seamless visual scaling.

questions.question: What does the media query '@media (hover: hover)' detect?
questions.a: Whether the user is currently hovering
questions.b: Whether the primary input device of the system has a true hover capability (like a desktop mouse), distinguishing desktop from touchscreens
questions.explanation: hover: hover detects pointing devices (mice), while hover: none identifies touch devices.

questions.question: What does '@media (pointer: coarse)' detect?
questions.b: A primary pointing device with limited precision, such as a user's finger on a mobile touchscreen, requiring larger 44px+ tap targets
questions.explanation: pointer: coarse identifies touch screens needing enlarged interactive hit areas.

questions.question: What is the recommended minimum tap target size for touch buttons under WCAG mobile accessibility guidelines?
questions.b: At least 44px by 44px (or 48px by 48px)
questions.explanation: WCAG 2.5.5 recommends minimum 44x44px touch targets to prevent mis-clicks.

questions.question: What does '@media (resolution: 2dppx)' (or -webkit-min-device-pixel-ratio: 2) detect?
questions.b: High-DPI / High-Resolution Retina displays with 2 or more physical device pixels per CSS pixel, used to serve crisp 2x image assets
questions.explanation: dppx media queries serve high-density @2x/@3x raster artwork to Retina screens.

questions.question: What does '@media (prefers-contrast: more)' detect?
questions.b: Whether the user has enabled High Contrast mode in accessibility settings, requiring distinct borders and high contrast color ratios
questions.explanation: prefers-contrast enhances UI readability for visually impaired users.

questions.question: What does 'env(safe-area-inset-top)' and 'env(safe-area-inset-bottom)' do on mobile devices (e.g. iPhones with notches / Dynamic Island)?
questions.a: Sets safe screen margins to prevent UI content from being occluded by hardware notches, rounded screen corners, and home indicator bars
questions.b: Calculates battery life
questions.explanation: env(safe-area-inset-*) pads UI around hardware camera notches and navigation home bars.

questions.question: Which viewport meta value is required to enable 'env(safe-area-inset-*)' on notched devices?
questions.b: notch-adapt=true
questions.explanation: viewport-fit=cover expands webpage rendering behind hardware notches for safe area padding.

questions.question: What is the primary benefit of designing with relative units (rem, %, ch) instead of fixed pixels (px) for layouts and typography?
questions.a: Relative units automatically scale when users adjust their default browser font size for accessibility, preventing layout breakage
questions.b: Pixels do not work on smartphones
questions.explanation: Relative units respect user accessibility font-scaling preferences.

questions.question: What does the HTML '<picture>' element combined with CSS provide for responsive images?
questions.b: Art direction and format switching (serving WebP/AVIF to modern browsers and cropped square images to mobile screens via <source media=\'...\'>)
questions.explanation: The <picture> element serves tailored crop ratios and next-gen image formats based on media queries.

questions.question: What does the HTML 'srcset' and 'sizes' attribute on an tag accomplish?
questions.a: Allows the browser to automatically select and download the optimal image file resolution based on device DPI and current layout display width
questions.b: Sets image border size
questions.explanation: srcset/sizes optimizes bandwidth by letting browsers download exact resolution matches.

questions.question: How are CSS Custom Properties (CSS Variables) declared syntactically?
questions.a: With two leading hyphens (e.g. '--primary-color: #3B82F6;') on a selector like :root
questions.b: With a dollar sign ($primary-color)
questions.explanation: CSS custom properties require two leading dashes (e.g. --brand-color).
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: How do you access and consume the value of a CSS Custom Property in a declaration?
questions.b: Using $variableName
questions.explanation: var(--name, fallback) retrieves the custom property value.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: How do you provide a fallback value if a CSS variable is undefined?
questions.a: var(--brand-color, #10B981) (the second argument inside var() acts as the fallback)
questions.b: var(--brand-color) || #10B981
questions.explanation: var() accepts optional comma-separated fallback values if the token is missing.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: Are CSS Custom Properties scoped and cascaded through the DOM tree, or are they purely global?
questions.b: They are fully scoped and cascaded through the DOM tree; variables declared on a parent or component class are inherited by its children and can be overridden locally
questions.explanation: CSS variables adhere to full cascade and inheritance scoping rules.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: Can CSS Custom Properties be read and dynamically updated at runtime using JavaScript?
questions.b: Yes, using 'element.style.setProperty('--color', val)' and 'getComputedStyle(element).getPropertyValue('--color')'
questions.c: Only by reloading the entire stylesheet
questions.explanation: CSS variables integrate seamlessly with JS runtime DOM style mutations.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: Which CSS property applies visual graphic effects (like blur, grayscale, contrast) to an element's rendered output?
questions.b: graphic-effect
questions.explanation: The 'filter' property applies Photoshop-style raster effects to elements.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'filter: blur(10px);' do to an element or image?
questions.b: Applies a 10px Gaussian blur effect over the entire element
questions.c: Blurs the background behind the element
questions.explanation: filter: blur() applies a Gaussian blur to the element itself.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What is the key difference between 'filter: blur()' and 'backdrop-filter: blur()'?
questions.b: 'filter: blur()' blurs the element itself; 'backdrop-filter: blur()' blurs the underlying content BEHIND a semi-transparent element (Glassmorphism effect)
questions.explanation: backdrop-filter blurs background layers visible through frosted-glass containers.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: How is the popular 'Glassmorphism / Frosted Glass' UI visual card effect created in modern CSS?
questions.a: background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.2); backdrop-filter: blur(12px); border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.3);
questions.b: filter: glass(100%);
questions.explanation: Semi-transparent background + backdrop-filter blur + subtle light border creates the glassmorphic aesthetic.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'filter: grayscale(100%);' do?
questions.b: Converts the element/image completely into black and white (monochrome grayscale)
questions.explanation: grayscale(100%) removes all color saturation, rendering pure black and white.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'filter: drop-shadow(0 4px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.5));' do on a transparent PNG or SVG icon?
questions.a: Casts a rectangular shadow around the bounding box
questions.b: Casts a true contour shadow matching the exact non-transparent pixel silhouettes and shapes of the PNG/SVG graphic
questions.explanation: filter: drop-shadow follows the actual alpha mask contours of transparent PNGs and SVGs.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'filter: hue-rotate(90deg);' do?
questions.a: Rotates the element physically by 90 degrees
questions.b: Shifts all color hues around the color wheel by 90 degrees (transforming blue to purple, green to yellow, etc.)
questions.explanation: hue-rotate() shifts color palette angles around the 360-degree color circle.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'filter: invert(100%);' achieve?
questions.b: Inverts all color values to their exact opposite mathematical complements (white becomes black, blue becomes orange, etc.)
questions.explanation: invert(100%) produces photo-negative color inversions.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'mix-blend-mode: multiply;' do in CSS?
questions.b: Blends the element's content colors with the colors of the underlying elements beneath it using the Multiply blend mode algorithm (darkening layers)
questions.explanation: mix-blend-mode composites overlapping DOM elements using Photoshop blending modes.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'background-blend-mode: overlay;' do on a container with both a background image and a background color?
questions.a: Blends the background image with the background color layer on the same element using the Overlay blending mode
questions.b: Deletes the background image
questions.explanation: background-blend-mode blends multiple background image and color layers on a single element.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does the modern CSS '@property' at-rule (Houdini API) allow developers to do?
questions.a: Register custom properties with explicit types (syntax: '<color>'), initial values, and inheritance flags, enabling CSS variables to be smoothly animated
questions.b: Create JavaScript classes
questions.explanation: @property registers typed CSS variables with the browser, allowing gradients and custom tokens to interpolate in transitions.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'isolation: isolate;' do in CSS blend mode and stacking context architectures?
questions.a: Disables internet connectivity for the element
questions.b: Creates a new stacking context that stops 'mix-blend-mode' from blending into elements outside this container
questions.explanation: isolation: isolate traps blend modes within the container boundary.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'color-scheme: dark light;' declare in CSS?
questions.b: Informs the browser that the page supports both dark and light modes, enabling automatic theming of native browser scrollbars, form controls, and canvas
questions.explanation: color-scheme styles native browser scrollbars and inputs to match OS dark/light mode.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'scrollbar-gutter: stable;' prevent when dynamic content causes scrollbars to appear?
questions.b: Prevents layout shift (content jumping sideways) by reserving dedicated gutter space for the vertical scrollbar even when it is not currently needed
questions.explanation: scrollbar-gutter: stable eliminates annoying horizontal layout shifts when scrollbars toggle.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'scrollbar-width: thin;' and 'scrollbar-color: #3B82F6 transparent;' do in modern cross-browser CSS?
questions.a: Styles native browser scrollbars with custom colors and thickness without proprietary -webkit- scrollbar hacks
questions.b: Disables scrollbars
questions.explanation: Standard CSS scrollbar properties style scrollbar thumbs cleanly across modern browsers.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'scroll-behavior: smooth;' do when users click anchor links to navigate page sections?
questions.b: Smoothly animates the scrolling viewport motion to the targeted section ID instead of jumping abruptly
questions.explanation: scroll-behavior: smooth provides native smooth page scrolling animations.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'scroll-snap-type: x mandatory;' do on a horizontal carousel slider?
questions.b: Forces horizontal scroll containers to snap cleanly to designated child snap points whenever the user finishes scrolling or swiping
questions.explanation: scroll-snap-type implements native touch carousels without JavaScript libraries.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What property is placed on child items inside a snap container to define their alignment point?
questions.b: snap-to: center;
questions.explanation: scroll-snap-align specifies where cards lock within the visible viewport.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'scroll-padding-top: 80px;' on the <html> root element fix for anchor link navigation?
questions.a: Adds a top margin to body
questions.b: Offsets the anchor scroll target position by 80px, preventing fixed/sticky headers from obscuring the top of the navigated section
questions.explanation: scroll-padding accounts for sticky header height during URL anchor jumps.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'overscroll-behavior: contain;' prevent on mobile browsers?
questions.b: Prevents 'scroll chaining' and unwanted pull-to-refresh gestures when scrolling reaches the boundary of an inner modal dialog or dropdown
questions.explanation: overscroll-behavior: contain prevents inner modal scrolling from leaking into outer page scrolling.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'touch-action: pan-y;' do on mobile touchscreens?
questions.b: Enables vertical single-finger scrolling (pan-y) while disabling pinch-zoom and horizontal swipe gestures on that element
questions.explanation: touch-action optimizes mobile web apps and custom swipe components.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'image-rendering: pixelated;' do to small retro pixel art graphics when scaled up?
questions.a: Smooths and blurs pixels with bilinear interpolation
questions.b: Disables anti-aliasing smoothing, rendering crisp, sharp, blocky pixel edges (nearest-neighbor scaling)
questions.explanation: pixelated preserves sharp pixel art graphics without blurry interpolation.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does the CSS property 'caret-color: #3B82F6;' customize?
questions.b: The color of the blinking text insertion cursor inside editable inputs and textareas
questions.explanation: caret-color themes the blinking text input cursor.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'content-visibility: auto;' do for long, content-heavy web pages?
questions.b: Skips rendering and layout calculations for off-screen elements until they approach the viewport, dramatically boosting initial page load and rendering performance
questions.explanation: content-visibility: auto provides massive rendering speedups for long articles and feeds.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What does 'contain-intrinsic-size' do when combined with 'content-visibility: auto;'?
questions.b: Provides an estimated placeholder height/width for unrendered off-screen elements, preventing scrollbar jumpiness as they scroll into view
questions.explanation: contain-intrinsic-size reserves placeholder dimensions to maintain stable scrollbar sizing.
questions.moduleName: Modern CSS3: Custom Properties, Filters & Effects

questions.question: What is the key difference between a Media Query (@media) and a CSS Container Query (@container)?
questions.b: Media Queries evaluate the dimensions of the entire BROWSER VIEWPORT; Container Queries evaluate the dimensions of an individual PARENT CONTAINER component
questions.c: Container queries only work on flexbox
questions.d: Media queries only work on mobile
questions.explanation: Container queries allow components to adapt modularly based on their immediate container space.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: Which CSS property designates an element as a queryable container for Container Queries?
questions.b: container: true;
questions.explanation: container-type: inline-size establishes a container context for width-based queries.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does '@container (min-width: 400px)' do to a component inside a defined container?
questions.a: Applies styles to the component when its parent container is at least 400px wide, regardless of total browser screen width
questions.b: Resizes the browser window
questions.d: Applies styles to the entire page
questions.explanation: Container queries style cards based on parent container width (e.g. sidebar vs main grid placement).
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What do the Container Query Units 'cqw' and 'cqh' represent in CSS?
questions.b: 1% of the query container's width (cqw) and 1% of the query container's height (cqh)
questions.explanation: cqw and cqh provide proportional fluid units relative to parent container dimensions.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is Native CSS Nesting (CSS Nesting Module)?
questions.a: A feature requiring Sass or SCSS preprocessors
questions.b: Standard browser capability to nest child CSS rules and pseudo-classes directly inside parent rule blocks using the '&' nesting selector natively
questions.explanation: Native CSS Nesting enables hierarchical rule nesting directly in vanilla CSS without preprocessors.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: In Native CSS Nesting, what does the '&' (ampersand) symbol represent?
questions.b: The Parent Selector, referring to the outer enclosing rule selector (e.g. '&:hover' or '&.active')
questions.explanation: '&' references the parent selector in nested CSS rule blocks.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the CSS '@layer' rule (Cascade Layers) solve in large-scale web architecture?
questions.b: Provides explicit control over cascade priority and stylesheet layering order (e.g. @layer reset, base, components, utilities) independent of selector specificity
questions.explanation: Cascade Layers (@layer) organize cascade hierarchy so utilities override components regardless of specificity.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: In Cascade Layers declared as '@layer base, components, utilities;', which layer has the highest precedence and wins conflicts?
questions.b: @layer utilities (the LAST declared layer in the cascade order has highest priority)
questions.d: The layer with the highest specificity
questions.explanation: Layers listed later in layer order take precedence over earlier layers in normal declarations.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is BEM (Block, Element, Modifier) in CSS methodology?
questions.b: A naming convention methodology (e.g. .card, .card__title, .card--featured) for writing modular, reusable, and collision-free CSS classes
questions.explanation: BEM (Block__Element--Modifier) structures clean, maintainable class architectures.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: In BEM naming conventions, what does two underscores '__' represent (e.g. '.card__header')?
questions.b: An Element (a child part of the Block component)
questions.explanation: Double underscore (__) designates an internal Element of a Block.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: In BEM naming conventions, what does two hyphens '--' represent (e.g. '.btn--primary')?
questions.b: A Modifier (representing a variant, theme, or state of a Block or Element)
questions.explanation: Double hyphen (--) represents a Modifier state or style variation.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is Utility-First CSS architecture (such as Tailwind CSS or custom utility systems)?
questions.a: Writing thousands of lines of custom semantic CSS classes for every HTML element
questions.b: Composing UI designs directly in HTML using low-level, single-purpose utility classes (e.g. 'flex', 'p-4', 'text-center', 'rounded-lg')
questions.c: Using inline styles on every element
questions.explanation: Utility-First CSS composes modular atomic classes directly in markup.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is 'Critical CSS' in web performance optimization?
questions.a: CSS code that has syntax errors
questions.b: The minimal set of CSS required to render the above-the-fold content of a page, inlined directly into HTML <head> to eliminate render-blocking stylesheet requests
questions.explanation: Inlining Critical CSS accelerates First Contentful Paint (FCP) and Largest Contentful Paint (LCP).
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'PurgeCSS' or CSS Tree-Shaking do during a production build step?
questions.b: Scans HTML and JS templates to find and remove all unused CSS selectors and classes from the final compiled stylesheet bundle
questions.explanation: CSS Purging strips unused classes, drastically reducing stylesheet payload sizes.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the '@scope' at-rule do in modern CSS?
questions.b: Applies CSS styles strictly within a designated DOM subtree boundary, preventing styles from leaking out or penetrating beyond lower scope limits
questions.explanation: @scope creates DOM boundary limits for style encapsulation without Shadow DOM.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is the 'Shadow DOM' and how does it achieve style encapsulation in Web Components?
questions.b: An isolated DOM subtree attached to an element where internal CSS styles are completely encapsulated and cannot leak out to or be affected by global page styles
questions.explanation: Shadow DOM creates sealed component boundaries with scoped CSS rules.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is the CSS pseudo-class ':host' used for inside Shadow DOM stylesheets?
questions.b: Selects and styles the custom element host container that contains the shadow tree (e.g. ':host(:hover)')
questions.explanation: :host targets the custom element host from within Shadow DOM.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the '::part()' pseudo-element allow external stylesheets to do to Shadow DOM components?
questions.b: Selects and styles specific exposed internal elements of a Shadow DOM component tagged with \'part="..."\' without breaking encapsulation
questions.explanation: ::part() exposes explicit customization hooks in encapsulated Web Components.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is 'CSS-in-JS' (e.g. Styled Components, Emotion) in modern frontend frameworks (React/Vue)?
questions.a: Writing raw HTML in CSS files
questions.b: A paradigm where component styles are authored directly within JavaScript/TypeScript code using tagged template literals, generating scoped classes dynamically
questions.explanation: CSS-in-JS co-locates styles with components in JS/TS ecosystems.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What are 'CSS Modules' (e.g. 'Button.module.css')?
questions.b: CSS files where all class names are automatically scoped locally by compilation tooling (generating unique hashes like 'Button_btn__a8f3d') to prevent global class collisions
questions.explanation: CSS Modules scope class names locally by compiling unique hashed class identifiers.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the 'page-break-inside: avoid;' (or 'break-inside: avoid;') property do in print stylesheets?
questions.b: Prevents a table, card, or chart from being split/severed across two separate printed pages
questions.explanation: break-inside: avoid prevents awkward pagination splits through cards or tables in print output.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'break-before: page;' do in print styling?
questions.b: Forces a clean page break before the element, ensuring it begins at the top of a new printed sheet
questions.explanation: break-before: page starts major headings and chapters on fresh print pages.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is 'CSS Specificity Wars' and how do modern architectures solve it?
questions.b: A code maintainability anti-pattern where developers endlessly chain IDs, classes, and !important to override styles; solved by BEM, Utility-First, or @layer cascades
questions.explanation: Specificity wars are mitigated by low-specificity architectures (BEM, Cascade Layers).
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does '@media (forced-colors: active)' detect (Windows High Contrast Mode)?
questions.b: Whether the operating system has enabled Forced Colors / High Contrast mode, restricting colors to a limited user-defined palette
questions.explanation: forced-colors: active ensures critical borders and icons remain visible in system high contrast modes.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'text-wrap: balance;' do in modern CSS typography?
questions.b: Automatically balances the number of words on each line of headlines and titles, preventing unsightly lone single-word dangling lines ('orphans/widows')
questions.explanation: text-wrap: balance creates harmonious, aesthetically balanced multi-line headings.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'text-wrap: pretty;' do?
questions.a: Adds decorative rainbow colors to text
questions.b: Optimizes line-breaking algorithms to eliminate typographical orphan words on the final line of body paragraphs
questions.explanation: text-wrap: pretty prevents solitary orphan words on trailing paragraph lines.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does the ':dir(rtl)' pseudo-class do in internationalized multi-lingual layouts?
questions.b: Matches and styles elements whose text direction is explicitly Right-to-Left (e.g. Arabic, Hebrew) without requiring manual class toggles
questions.explanation: :dir(rtl) styles directionality dynamically based on document language semantics.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'font-synthesis: none;' prevent the browser from doing?
questions.b: Synthesizing fake, artificially skewed bold or italic versions of a font when the true bold/italic font weights are missing from the downloaded font family
questions.explanation: font-synthesis: none disables ugly browser-generated fake bold/italic typefaces.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What is the 'Golden Rule' of modern maintainable CSS architecture?
questions.b: Keep specificity as low and flat as possible, design mobile-first with relative units, embrace the cascade, and compose reusable design tokens
questions.c: Write all styles as inline HTML attributes
questions.explanation: Flat specificity, modular tokens, and semantic layout systems guarantee long-term codebase maintainability.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts

questions.question: What does 'light-dark(#ffffff, #121212)' function do in CSS Color Module Level 5?
questions.b: Returns the first color in Light mode and the second color in Dark mode automatically based on the active 'color-scheme' context
questions.explanation: light-dark(lightColor, darkColor) automatically yields the proper color according to color-scheme.
questions.moduleName: CSS Architecture, Container Queries & Modern Layouts
